signals.source_name: California Assembly Committee on Human Services
signals.summary: California Assembly Bill 1899 would establish an Office of Youth Homelessness Prevention within the California Interagency Council on Homelessness to reduce youth homelessness to functional zero. The Office would develop a comprehensive framework with measurable goals including decreasing homelessness within 12 months of discharge from foster care and other public systems, and coordinating funding across child welfare, foster care, juvenile justice, and behavioral health agencies. A publicly accessible dashboard would track progress.
signals.why_it_matters: California has the largest youth population of any US state and one of the highest rates of youth homelessness. This bill would create the first dedicated state-level institutional home for youth homelessness prevention in California, addressing a structural gap where youth exiting foster care face predictable homelessness due to fragmented responsibility across multiple systems.

signals.title: Council of Europe YOUthDIG 2026 Links Internet Governance to Social and Environmental Justice Ahead of EuroDIG
signals.summary: The Youth Dialogue on Internet Governance 2026 was held from 23-25 May 2026 in Brussels as a pre-event to EuroDIG 2026. Young participants aged 18-30 from across the pan-European region engaged in capacity-building on digital policy and drafted the 2026 YOUthDIG Messages, which stress that Internet governance is inseparable from social and environmental justice and from strengthening democratic resilience. The event marked 20 years of .eu as a trusted digital identity.
signals.why_it_matters: YOUthDIG demonstrates sustained institutional commitment to embedding youth voices in Internet governance, directly linking youth digital policy capacity-building to the formal EuroDIG multi-stakeholder platform. The 2026 Messages' framing of Internet governance as inseparable from social and environmental justice represents an evolution in youth digital rights advocacy that connects digital policy to climate and equity concerns.

signals.title: India Introduces Constitutional Amendment for 33% Women's Reservation Linked to Historic Delimitation and Seat Expansion
signals.summary: The Indian government introduced three Constitution Amendment Bills in the Lok Sabha on 16 April 2026 including the 131st Amendment Bill to operationalise 33% reservation for women and a Delimitation Bill to redraw constituency boundaries. The Lok Sabha would expand from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats to accommodate the quota. While the 131st Amendment Bill failed its final vote, a redrafted version is expected in the monsoon session starting July 2026.
signals.why_it_matters: This represents India's most significant electoral restructuring since independence, linking women's parliamentary representation to comprehensive delimitation for the first time. The precedent of using constitutional quotas to reshape legislative composition is directly relevant to youth representation debates. The expansion of Lok Sabha seats from 543 to 850 would be the largest increase in parliamentary capacity in Indian history.

signals.title: Liberia Launches National Youth Digital Transformation Initiative With 15 Digital Skills Hubs Under OGP Commitment
signals.source_name: Open Government Partnership / Government of Liberia
signals.summary: Liberia's Ministry of Youth and Sports and the Liberia Telecommunications Authority launched 15 Youth Digital Skills Hubs across the country, providing computers, Starlink broadband, and a three-month training program for approximately 750 young people. The initiative, part of Liberia's Open Government Partnership commitment, aims to increase youth participation in governance by 50%, establish an open data portal for youth policymaking input, and strengthen digital literacy as a foundation for civic engagement.
signals.why_it_matters: This is a concrete national implementation of the digital inclusion and youth governance agenda, linking digital capacity-building directly to open government and intergenerational policy participation. The explicit target of 50% increased youth governance participation makes it a measurable, trackable signal of how digital inclusion can operationalise intergenerational equity in a low-income, youth-bulge country context.

signals.title: UK Government Launches 2.5 Billion Youth Guarantee With 3,000 Youth Jobs Grant and Expanded Job Guarantee
signals.summary: DWP published version 3 of the 2026 to 2027 apprenticeship funding rules on 29 July 2026, applying to starts from 1 August 2026 to 31 July 2027 under the Growth and Skills Levy. For new starts, government funds 100% of training and assessment (up to the funding-band maximum) for apprentices aged 16-24 at non-levy employers, and the same 100% cover applies where a levy payer has insufficient Apprenticeship Service funds. Co-investment for 25+ non-levy starts stays at 5%; levy payers with insufficient funds pay 25% for 25+ starts. From 1 October 2026, non-levy employers can claim a £2,000 hiring payment for new 16-24 apprentices who started the job within the previous three months, paid in two instalments after 90 days, stackable with the £3,000 Youth Jobs Grant for 18-24 Universal Credit claimants. The employer-schemes page states the 16-24 full-funding rule covers both levy and non-levy employers.
signals.why_it_matters: This is the UK's most ambitious youth employment intervention in a generation, responding to youth unemployment reaching a five-year high in late 2025. The combination of hiring subsidies, guaranteed employment, and apprenticeship incentives represents a comprehensive demand-side approach to youth labour market integration. The scale makes it a significant test of whether targeted employer subsidies can effectively reduce youth unemployment without displacement.

sightings.source_name: UK Department for Work and Pensions

signals.title: Council of EU Approves Revised Youth Strategy Work Plan 2025-2027 Focusing on Post-2027 Successor and Youth Mainstreaming
signals.summary: The Council of the European Union approved a revised EU Youth Strategy Work Plan 2025-2027 on 11 May 2026 covering the work of the Poland-Denmark-Cyprus and Ireland-Lithuania-Greece Presidency Trios. The revision prioritises preparation for the post-2027 EU Youth Strategy including a listening and co-creation process with youth stakeholders, review of the European Youth Goals, and the 11th and 12th cycles of the EU Youth Dialogue.
signals.why_it_matters: This revision comes at a pivotal moment as the current EU Youth Strategy approaches its end, making the decisions taken now about its successor critical for shaping European youth governance for the next decade. The emphasis on youth mainstreaming across all policy areas reflects a maturing approach from youth-specific programs to embedding youth perspectives in all EU policymaking.

signals.title: IMF Fiscal Monitor Warns Global Public Debt on Path to 100% of GDP by 2029, Earlier Than Previously Forecast
signals.summary: The IMF's April 2026 Fiscal Monitor warns global public debt rose to nearly 94% of GDP in 2025 and is projected to reach 100% by 2029, a year earlier than previously forecast. The report titled 'Fiscal Policy under Pressure: High Debt, Rising Risks' highlights that trade fragmentation, geopolitical tensions, and higher interest rates have structurally altered the fiscal environment, urging immediate consolidation measures.
signals.why_it_matters: Sovereign debt accumulated today represents a direct claim on future taxpayers' income. The IMF's accelerated debt trajectory means younger generations face higher tax burdens or reduced public services to service debts they did not incur. The report explicitly links delay in adjustment to more disruptive measures later, underscoring the intergenerational stakes of current fiscal choices.

signals.title: OECD Global Debt Report Finds Sovereign Bond Markets Reached Record $61 Trillion With Rising Refinancing Risk
signals.summary: The OECD Global Debt Report 2026 finds OECD sovereign debt reached a record $61 trillion in 2025 with projected gross borrowing of $29 trillion in 2026, a 17% increase over 2024. Treasury bills now account for 48% of total borrowing, dramatically increasing rollover exposure and refinancing risk. The report warns debt market resilience is not guaranteed.
signals.why_it_matters: Record sovereign borrowing levels and shorter maturities transfer refinancing risk to future cohorts. The report warns that fiscal prudence is needed to avoid crowding out private investment, including an estimated $4.1 trillion in AI-driven capital expenditure from 2026-2030, which affects future economic opportunity. Current borrowing decisions will shape the fiscal space available to younger generations.

signals.title: France Suspends Planned Increase of Retirement Age to 64, Deferring Pension Fiscal Adjustment After 2027 Election
signals.summary: The French National Assembly voted 255-146 on October 12, 2025 to suspend the planned increase of the retirement age for a full pension to 64 years and the increase of the standard retirement age from 67 to 68. The suspension postpones a decision until after the 2027 presidential election. The cost is estimated at 300 million euros in 2026 and 1.9 billion euros in 2027, to be offset through other austerity measures.
signals.why_it_matters: France's suspension of pension age increases in the context of an EU excessive deficit procedure represents a choice to defer fiscal adjustment, pushing the financing burden onto future taxpayers. The French Court of Auditors had warned the system lacks intragenerational fairness, with longer life expectancy for higher-income workers meaning retirement age increases affect groups unequally.

signals.title: UK Inheritance Tax Receipts Hit Record 8.25 Billion as Frozen Thresholds Drive Fiscal Drag Across Generations
signals.summary: UK inheritance tax receipts reached 8.25 billion pounds in 2024-25, a 700 million pound increase from the previous record. The IHT threshold has been frozen at 325,000 pounds since 2009. OBR estimates show IHT raising 14.5 billion pounds annually by 2030-31 under current thresholds. Combined with pensions entering IHT from 2027 and new relief rules for business assets, the IHT system is undergoing its most significant reshaping in decades.
signals.why_it_matters: Frozen IHT thresholds represent a stealth tax increase that pulls middle-class estates into the tax net. This is a direct intergenerational transfer from inheritors to the state, with the government projected to double current IHT revenue by 2030. The policy choices around which assets receive relief shape which families can transmit wealth across generations.

signals.title: US One Big Beautiful Bill Act Permanently Sets Federal Estate Tax Exemption at $15 Million Per Person
signals.summary: Signed into law on July 4, 2025, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act permanently increases the federal estate and gift tax exemption to $15 million per person indexed for inflation from 2027. This prevents the scheduled sunset that would have reverted the exemption to approximately $7 million. The top estate tax rate remains 40%.
signals.why_it_matters: A permanent $15 million exemption means over 99.5% of estates pay zero federal estate tax, dramatically narrowing the wealth transfer tax base. This policy choice concentrates intergenerational wealth transmission among the wealthiest families without taxation, potentially exacerbating dynastic wealth accumulation at a time of historically large intergenerational wealth transfers estimated at $84 trillion over the next two decades.

signals.title: India Includes 10,000 Crore in Sovereign Green Bonds in H2 2025-26 Borrowing Plan Amid Green Finance Taxonomy Push
signals.source_name: Department of Economic Affairs, Government of India
signals.summary: The Indian government announced a borrowing plan of 6.77 lakh crore for H2 FY2025-26, including 10,000 crore through Sovereign Green Bonds. The government is also considering tax breaks for green bond buyers amid declining investor interest, and a Climate Finance Taxonomy is expected to expand eligible expenditure categories to include industrial transition activities.
signals.why_it_matters: India's sovereign green bond programme represents a mechanism for shifting climate capital costs across generations, using debt to finance renewable energy and clean transport whose benefits accrue long-term. The criticism that the programme funds existing projects rather than new climate action raises questions about whether it constitutes genuine intergenerational investment or greenwashing of routine fiscal operations.

signals.title: OECD Croatia Economic Survey Recommends Housing Tax Reform to Address Intergenerational Equity
signals.summary: The OECD Economic Survey on Croatia recommends extending recurrent taxes on immovable property to all homeowners and basing them on regularly updated market values. It also recommends phasing out transaction taxes and capital gains exemptions that bias toward homeownership, and introducing a recurrent tax on vacant properties and short-term rentals.
signals.why_it_matters: Housing tax design directly shapes intergenerational opportunity: property tax exemptions and transaction tax relief for older owners effectively subsidise wealth accumulation in housing, while first-time buyers face rising prices and limited access. The OECD's recommendations aim to make housing taxation more equitable across generations while protecting asset-rich, income-poor elderly through tax deferrals.

signals.title: UK Welfare Trends Report Reveals Universal Credit Fraud at 7.4 Billion as Working-Age Benefits Face Cuts While Pensions Protected
signals.source_name: UK Department for Work and Pensions
signals.summary: DWP's Welfare Trends Report reveals Universal Credit overpayments reached 7.4 billion pounds in 2025-26, with 81% classified as fraud. Total welfare overpayments stood at 10.3 billion pounds. The report notes that welfare spending cuts are concentrated on working-age benefits while pensioner benefits remain protected through the triple lock.
signals.why_it_matters: The divergence in treatment between working-age welfare being cut and pensioner benefits protected by the triple lock represents a significant intergenerational transfer: younger cohorts facing reduced support and higher National Insurance contributions are funding inflation-protected pensions for retirees. The 10.3 billion in overpayments also represents a fiscal leakage that must eventually be recovered from future tax revenue.

signals.title: India's 16th Finance Commission Debates Tax Devolution Formula With Major Implications for Inter-State Youth Opportunity
signals.summary: The Sixteenth Finance Commission of India is debating how far tax devolution should correct inter-state inequality versus reward economic performance. The formula determines the vertical and horizontal distribution of central tax revenues to states, affecting resource allocation for public services including education, health, and infrastructure that shape opportunity for younger generations in different states.
signals.why_it_matters: Fiscal federalism decisions about tax devolution directly determine which regions' youth have access to public goods and services. A formula favouring equity directs more resources to poorer states with younger populations, while one favouring performance rewards wealthier states. This is an intergenerational issue because today's devolution formula shapes the human capital and economic opportunity set for the next generation across Indian states.

signals.title: Realtor.com Research Finds 1 in 5 First-Time US Homebuyers Rely on Parental Housing Equity
signals.summary: Realtor.com research finds that 1 in 5 first-time buyers have parents extracting equity from their own homes to finance their children's purchases. The research connects rising home prices and higher mortgage rates to increased reliance on intergenerational wealth transfers for homeownership access, exacerbating the gap between those with and without wealthy parents.
signals.why_it_matters: When homeownership access increasingly depends on parental wealth rather than earned income, housing markets become mechanisms for transmitting inequality across generations rather than equalising opportunity. The report underscores how housing tax policy including mortgage interest deduction and capital gains exemptions disproportionately benefits existing homeowners, compounding the advantage for children of homeowners over children of renters.

signals.title: UN Economist Network Releases Governance Futures Policy Brief Exploring Alternative Governance Models for 2040
signals.summary: The UN Economist Network released a Futures and Foresight Policy Brief examining limitations of current governance systems and proposing alternative models for 2040. Using strategic foresight, it analyzed drivers of change across political, economic, social, technological, and environmental domains to chart pathways toward adaptive, inclusive governance. The brief explores scenarios ranging from baseline incremental change to radical AI-augmented democracy.
signals.why_it_matters: This is one of the UN system's most advanced institutional foresight exercises on governance reform, directly feeding into UN 2.0 and the broader modernization agenda. Its governance scenarios provide a framework that youth organizations and intergenerational equity advocates can leverage to argue for anticipatory governance reforms that protect long-term interests.

signals.title: OECD Launches Comprehensive Strategic Foresight Toolkit for Resilient Public Policy With 25 Disruption Briefings
signals.summary: The OECD published a comprehensive 172-page Strategic Foresight Toolkit featuring a five-step foresight methodology with facilitation guides, case studies from pilots in New Zealand, Philippines, Canada, Indonesia, and Lithuania, and briefings on 25 potential disruptions across environmental, technological, economic, social, and geopolitical domains. The toolkit is designed to help policymakers challenge assumptions, create scenarios, stress-test strategies, and develop actionable plans for sustainable public policy.
signals.why_it_matters: This is the first time the OECD has produced a hands-on operational foresight toolkit for government practitioners, not just analysis. It makes foresight methodology accessible to non-specialist policymakers with a standardised approach that can be adopted across different national contexts, significantly lowering the barrier to entry for governments wanting to build futures-thinking capacity.

signals.title: UN DESA World Population Highlights 2026 Projects 69% of World Youth Will Live in Low-Income Countries by 2050
signals.summary: UN DESA's World Population Highlights 2026 dedicated to youth reports that 69% of the world's youth will live in low- and lower-middle-income countries by 2050, up from 59% today. The report identifies priority actions to reduce disparities, promote sustainable livelihoods, improve health outcomes, and strengthen protection of young people's rights, supporting the Youth2030 UN system-wide strategy.
signals.why_it_matters: The concentration of youth in the world's poorest countries is a demographic megatrend with profound governance implications. It underscores the urgency of intergenerational equity frameworks that address the geographic mismatch between aging wealthy nations and youth-burgeoning developing countries, where education, employment, and health investments must be prioritised.

signals.title: Stimson Center Issue Brief Connects Demographic Trends to US National Security and Foreign Policy
signals.summary: The Stimson Center's Environmental Security Program issue brief examines how youth bulges, urbanization, aging, and immigration reshape US priorities. It notes the US is older than ever with only 7,300 geriatricians against a need of 30,000 by 2030, while Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia have record youth entering unprepared labour markets. The brief argues the 21st century is 'the demographic century' requiring cross-departmental strategic response.
signals.why_it_matters: This brief directly connects demographic trends to US foreign policy and national security, framing aging as a strategic issue rather than just social policy. It provides evidence that the intergenerational fiscal burden of aging populations has national security implications, requiring coordinated interagency strategy that accounts for divergent youth and elderly demographics across regions.

signals.title: UNESCO Global Education Monitoring Report 2026 Finds 273 Million Out of School and Introduces Equitable Financing Index
signals.summary: The 2026 GEM Report, first in a three-part Countdown to 2030 series, finds 273 million children and youth are out of school globally. It introduces the Equitable Financing in Education Index showing fewer than 1 in 10 countries have a strong equity focus in education financing. Only 24% of countries now have inclusive education laws, up from 1% in 2000.
signals.why_it_matters: This report shifts the global priority from enrollment to equity in learning outcomes, introducing a new metric for cross-country comparison of financing equity. The countdown framework creates accountability pressure ahead of the 2030 SDG deadline. The Equitable Financing Index provides a governance tool that directly measures intergenerational fairness in education investment.

signals.title: UNESCO-UNEVOC Global Youth Survey Finds 62% Use AI but Only 30% Have Received Formal Digital Skills Training
signals.summary: A global survey of 4,268 young people across 128 countries found 62% already use AI in real-world contexts but only 30% have received formal AI or digital skills training. 40% have not been taught about ethical AI use, 24% lack reliable connectivity, and 72% want to shape AI policies but lack opportunity for involvement. The survey reveals a significant gap between informal AI adoption and formal training infrastructure.
signals.why_it_matters: This is the largest global youth survey on AI skills perception, revealing an urgent intergenerational equity gap: young people are adopting AI informally while formal education systems fail to provide necessary skills training. The finding that 72% want AI policy involvement but are excluded highlights a democratic deficit in AI governance that intergenerational fairness frameworks must address.

signals.title: IBM Center for Business of Government Report Provides Blueprint for Embedding Strategic Foresight Into Government Planning
signals.source_name: IBM Center for The Business of Government
signals.summary: Professor Bert George's report analyses the disconnect between strategic foresight activities and ongoing strategic planning in government, using cases from Flanders, Singapore, the EU, and the US. It provides evidence-based guidance on governance structures, capabilities, and processes that enable sustainable integration of foresight into government operations, bridging the gap between futures units and core planning machinery.
signals.why_it_matters: This report addresses a critical governance gap: foresight units exist in many governments but remain siloed from core strategic planning. Its systems perspective and cross-country case analysis provide a practical blueprint for institutionalising foresight within the machinery of government, essential for durable intergenerational governance beyond episodic horizon scanning exercises.

signals.title: Portugal Intergenerational Justice Index Report 12 Updates Methodology Across Six Dimensions of Fairness Between Generations
signals.source_name: Institute of Public Policy / Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation
signals.summary: The 12th report of the Intergenerational Justice Index for Portugal updates the methodology and results across six dimensions: housing, labour market, environment, public finances, health, inequality, and poverty. The index provides an annual composite measure for regular monitoring of intergenerational fairness in Portuguese public policy, making it one of the most systematic national-level intergenerational justice measurement tools globally.
signals.why_it_matters: Portugal's index is among the world's most systematic national-level intergenerational justice measurement tools. Its annual update cycle creates accountability pressure and enables evidence-based advocacy for policy reforms that balance generational interests. The six-dimensional methodology covering both fiscal and non-fiscal domains provides a replicable model for other countries developing intergenerational equity metrics.

signals.title: Sri Lanka Launches Updated National Policy for Senior Citizens as One of Fastest-Aging Developing Nations in Asia
signals.summary: Sri Lanka launched its updated National Policy for Senior Citizens 2025-2035 on the International Day of Older Persons, replacing the original 2006 policy. The policy addresses the rapid demographic shift from 12.4% elderly in 2012 to 18.3% in 2024, with projections of 25.04% by 2040. It covers 10 core areas including healthcare, social protection, elder rights, and active ageing across 51 specific actions.
signals.why_it_matters: Sri Lanka is aging faster than any South Asian country, yet its 2006 policy was outdated for decades. The 2025 revision provides a comprehensive framework for one of the most rapidly aging developing nations, offering lessons for Global South countries facing compressed demographic transitions where aging is occurring before reaching high income levels.

signals.title: Beyond GDP Global Alliance Enters Operational Phase at UN ECOSOC Forum With Over 30 Countries Endorsing
signals.summary: The Beyond GDP Global Alliance held its first plenary meeting at the UN ECOSOC Financing for Development Forum, marking its formal operational phase. Co-led by Spain, Uruguay, Senegal, OECD, UNCTAD, and SEGIB, with over 30 countries endorsing, the Alliance aims to embed multidimensional development metrics into development finance, planning, budgeting, and monitoring frameworks.
signals.why_it_matters: This moves Beyond GDP from academic discourse to operational international cooperation with a concrete governance mechanism. By connecting to the UN High-Level Expert Group on Beyond GDP and focusing on Global South engagement, it creates a vehicle to redefine how progress, prosperity, and intergenerational equity are measured in development finance and national planning.

signals.title: European Commission Develops Future-Oriented Policymaking Handbook and Training Package for Public Administrations
signals.source_name: European Commission (DG REFORM & JRC EU Policy Lab)
signals.summary: The European Commission's Future-Oriented Policymaking project, a joint initiative by DG REFORM and the JRC EU Policy Lab, announced its forthcoming handbook, online training series, and community building toolkit for embedding long-term thinking in public administrations. Beta-testing began spring 2026 with full package release expected after summer 2026, including case studies from Finland, Estonia, Singapore, Malta, and Spain.
signals.why_it_matters: This project directly implements the EU's Intergenerational Fairness Strategy by providing practical tools for foresight institutionalisation across all 27 Member States. It represents the EU's most ambitious attempt to make anticipatory governance a standard competency in public administration, creating a replicable training model that other regional bodies and national governments could adopt.

signals.title: World Bank Directors Declare Aging an Overlooked Mega-Trend With Three-Pillar Policy Framework
signals.summary: World Bank Directors Iffath Sharif and Juan Pablo Uribe published a blog post arguing aging is an overlooked mega-trend, noting developing economies age much faster than developed ones. They outline a three-pillar policy framework for healthy, prosperous, and dignified aging, and argue that developing countries face compressed demographic transitions that require immediate policy action before reaching high income levels.
signals.why_it_matters: The World Bank elevating aging to a core operational priority signals a major institutional shift in development finance. The three-pillar framework provides a coherent structure for integrating aging considerations into lending, technical assistance, and policy dialogue across the Bank's engagements in over 50 countries, creating leverage for intergenerational fiscal policy reforms.

signals.title: Indonesia Launches Lansia Berdaya Elderly Empowerment Program as 21 Provinces Enter Aging Phase
signals.source_name: ANTARA News / Ministry of Population and Family Development
signals.summary: Indonesia launched the Lansia Berdaya (Empowered Elderly) program as 12% of 286 million citizens are elderly and 21 provinces have entered an aging phase. The program includes health checks, family-based mentoring, senior schools, senior entrepreneur initiatives, and senior cards. BPJS Kesehatan spends Rp42 trillion ($2.52B) annually on elderly programs, reflecting the growing fiscal pressure of the demographic transition.
signals.why_it_matters: Indonesia is experiencing a compressed demographic transition while still developing, making its policy response a test case for middle-income countries facing aging before wealth. The Lansia Berdaya program's multi-component approach covering health, economic empowerment, and social inclusion offers a replicable model for aging policy in the Global South where institutional capacity is still developing.

signals.title: Ghana Heritage Fund Faces PRMA Reform Push as PIAC and NRGI Urge Safeguards for Future-Generations Savings
signals.summary: In a 2 June 2026 analysis, the Natural Resource Governance Institute reports that Ghana's Ministry of Finance is advancing amendments to expand eligible investment instruments for the Ghana Heritage Funds under the Petroleum Revenue Management Act framework — including energy-transition infrastructure — after parliamentary approval and pending presidential review. NRGI cites a 2026 technical roundtable co-hosted with the Public Interest and Accountability Committee (PIAC) at which the Bank of Ghana reported Petroleum Holding Funds of about US$1.376 billion. Separately, Ghana News Agency reported on 27 July 2026 that the Bank of Ghana's First Half-Year Report showed the Heritage Fund rising to US$1.46 billion by end-June 2026 (petroleum allocations plus investment income), reaffirming the fund's statutory purpose as a long-term savings mechanism for future generations after petroleum depletion.
signals.why_it_matters: This is a live stress test of a sovereign-wealth-style intergenerational instrument: whether resource windfalls stay ring-fenced for future cohorts or are redirected into near-term infrastructure under transition pressure. The mechanism memory is explicit — PRMA Heritage Fund / Stabilisation Fund architecture, PIAC oversight, and proposed instrument expansion — and the fairness logic is who bears the cost if long-term savings are diluted. Relationship memory: anchors the New Alignment IGS economic-instruments pillar example and sits alongside other intergenerational fiscal signals (Norway GPFG/tax reform, sovereign green bonds) as a Global South resource-fund case.

signals.title: NTI and The Elders Launch Intergenerational Dialogue on Biosecurity, Pandemic Preparedness, and Emerging Tech
signals.summary: On 26 March 2026 the Nuclear Threat Initiative and The Elders announced a high-level Intergenerational Dialogue on emerging technologies, pandemic preparedness, prevention and response (PPR), and global biosecurity governance. The programme convenes members of The Elders with early-career biosecurity leaders for an in-person UK dialogue in late October 2026, plus a field immersion with UK biosecurity institutions, preparatory remote sessions (July–September), a framing paper, and public-facing outputs through December 2026. It builds on NTI's Next Generation for Biosecurity project and The Elders' pandemic prevention work, explicitly targeting the intersection of AI, synthetic biology, and laboratory automation with health security and catastrophic biological risk.
signals.why_it_matters: This is a concrete operationalisation of intergenerational pairs on catastrophic biological risk — not consultation theatre, but a structured senior–next-gen governance dialogue with deliverables. Mechanism memory: Next Generation for Biosecurity + Elders dialogue + field immersion. Fairness logic: who designs biosecurity norms as dual-use AI/synbio barriers erode. Relationship memory: anchors New Alignment's proposed intergenerational-security pillar and participatory-structural instrument family; sits next to emerging-tech anticipatory governance.

signals.title: Canada Budget 2025 Creates C$2 Billion Critical Minerals Sovereign Fund for Strategic Supply-Chain Investments
signals.summary: Budget 2025 (tabled 4 November 2025) proposes C$2 billion over five years, cash basis, starting 2026-27, to Natural Resources Canada to create a Critical Minerals Sovereign Fund making strategic investments in critical minerals projects and companies — including equity investments, loan guarantees, and offtake agreements — plus C$50 million over five years for fund delivery. The measure sits inside a broader Critical Minerals Strategy and Major Projects Office agenda that links minerals to clean energy, advanced manufacturing, and defence/supply-chain resilience.
signals.why_it_matters: This is a sovereign-fund-style instrument framed primarily as national security and industrial strategy, not as a ring-fenced heritage savings vehicle for future generations (contrast Ghana PRMA Heritage Fund or Kenya's draft mineral IG fund). Mechanism memory: equity/loan-guarantee/offtake SWF-like facility under NRCan. Intergenerational stake: who captures mineral rents and environmental costs of extraction over decades, and whether 'sovereign fund' language IG-washes security industrial policy. Relationship memory: caution case in the New Alignment instrument taxonomy; future G20 Canada presidency relevance.

signals.title: EU AI Act Reaches Full Application of Core Obligations on 2 August 2026 Amid Omnibus High-Risk Stagger
signals.summary: On 20 July 2026 the Commission adopted Guidelines on implementing Article 50 transparency obligations of the AI Act (C(2026) 5054), 13 days before those obligations applied on 2 August 2026. The guidelines are a distinct implementation instrument, not a restatement of the already-ingested full-application timeline. For interactive AI (Art. 50(1)), providers must take account of children and other vulnerable groups whenever a system is intended or reasonably likely to interact with the public: notifications must be child-friendly, age-appropriate, easy to understand and accessible, including for children with disabilities; terms-and-conditions-only disclosures are insufficient. Periodic reminders are flagged as necessary for children, for sustained immersive use with addiction-like or emotional-dependency risk (explicitly including AI companions), and for health/legal/financial advice. Deployers of emotion-recognition and biometric-categorisation systems must inform everyone exposed, including children (Art. 50(3)). Deep-fake 'false appearance' assessments must consider child audiences with lower AI literacy. Horizontal Art. 50(5) rules require clear, distinguishable, first-interaction information that children can actually perceive. Fines can reach €15 million or 3% of worldwide turnover; national market-surveillance authorities lead enforcement.
signals.why_it_matters: This is the sharpest near-term binding AI governance lock-in for the New Alignment vision's Shift 2: institutions must shape systems in real time, not after the fact. signals.title: Alaska Governor Files HJR 30 to Constitutionalize Permanent Fund 5% POMV Draw and Automatic 50% Dividend
signals.summary: On 23 January 2026, House Rules by request of the Governor introduced HJR 30 (companion SJR 23), a proposed Alaska constitutional amendment on the Permanent Fund. The filed text would keep at least 25% of mineral revenues in the fund, cap annual withdrawals at 5% of a five-year average market-value (POMV) formula, require that 50% of the authorized withdrawal be paid automatically as dividends to eligible residents without appropriation, allow the remainder for government operations, fold the Earnings Reserve Account into principal by 30 June 2027, and place the amendments before voters at the next general election. As of the legislative journal, the measure was referred to House Finance and had not passed. Governor Dunleavy framed the package as permanently protecting the PFD after Wielechowski held that dividends must compete annually for appropriation.
signals.why_it_matters: Alaska’s Permanent Fund is the United States’ flagship nonrenewable-resource trust for future generations, yet the corpus currently tracks Montana/Hawaii trust and climate signals far more densely than Alaska fiscal design. Constitutionalizing a POMV spending rule plus an automatic 50/50 dividend–government split would lock in a durable intergenerational fiscal regime—and create a live tension between present per-capita consumption (PFD) and long-term corpus preservation that other state permanent funds (Minnesota school fund, New Mexico LGPF, North Dakota Legacy Fund) also face.

signals.title: Alaska Supreme Court Hears Sagoonick II Youth Challenge to State-Mandated Alaska LNG Project
signals.summary: On 4 March 2026, eight youth plaintiffs (ages 11–22), including Alaska Native youth, argued before the Alaska Supreme Court in Sagoonick v. The Anchorage Superior Court dismissed the case in March 2025 as a non-justiciable political question; plaintiffs seek reversal and remand for trial, arguing the North Slope-to-export LNG package would roughly triple Alaska greenhouse-gas emissions for decades. An affirmance would deepen the US pattern of state youth climate dismissals (Utah Natalie R., Wisconsin Dunn, Florida Reynolds); a reversal would reopen merits litigation against one of the largest proposed US fossil export projects and reinforce Article VIII public-trust framing for future generations.

signals.title: Czech President Vetoes Budget-Rules Reform Loosening National Fiscal Constraints Through 2036
signals.source_name: Office of the President of the Czech Republic
signals.summary: On 22 July 2026, President Petr Pavel returned to the Chamber of Deputies an amendment overhauling Czech budgetary-responsibility and budget-rules legislation. His veto letter argues the bill threatens long-term sustainability of public finances and weakens parliamentary oversight: it creates a 2026–2036 exemption from state-budget expenditure ceilings for Linear Act infrastructure (roads, rail, water, energy security) with no quantitative floor; extends the defence expenditure-ceiling exemption to 2036; and allows up to a 10% spending increase if the security situation worsens, including pathways that expand executive discretion relative to the Chamber. The Czech Fiscal Council’s Opinion No. 4/2026 (16 June 2026) had already warned that the package would leave governments bound mainly by EU fiscal rules and mark a ‘shift in the fiscal paradigm’ away from statutory paths toward 1.25%/1.00% of GDP structural deficits. Chamber override is scheduled for 25 August 2026; the ruling coalition says it has the votes.
signals.why_it_matters: This is the sharpest 2026 CEE institutional fight over intergenerational fiscal fairness: an independent fiscal council and the head of state explicitly frame expenditure-ceiling exemptions as transferring debt and interest burdens to future taxpayers, while government actors argue defence and infrastructure require the flexibility. Whatever the 25 August override outcome, the episode documents how national fiscal-responsibility architecture is being renegotiated under defence and investment pressure.

signals.title: Malaysia Dewan Rakyat Passes National Trust Fund Bill 2026 Recasting KWAN as Intergenerational Savings Vehicle
signals.summary: On 16 July 2026 Malaysia's Dewan Rakyat passed the National Trust Fund (Kumpulan Wang Amanah Negara, KWAN) Bill 2026 — the first comprehensive overhaul of the 1988 petroleum-linked national trust fund. Reforms create a National Trust Fund (Incorporated) statutory body to replace the existing panel (Bank Negara Malaysia continues administration during transition); introduce mandatory federal contributions of at least 0.1% of projected annual revenue plus 2% of Petronas dividends and 2% of depletable-resource export duties received by the federal government; cap annual withdrawals at 50% of expected long-term real return unless Dewan Rakyat approves a larger draw; and restrict uses to education, healthcare, and climate change mitigation and adaptation. signals.summary: On 29 May 2026, Poland's Sejm adopted the Act on the Rights and Duties of the Student (ustawa o prawach i obowiązkach ucznia). signals.title: Slovak Budget Council Finds Public Finances High-Risk and Shifting Burden to Future Generations
signals.summary: On 5 May 2026, Slovakia’s constitutional Council for Budget Responsibility published key conclusions of its Report on the Long-term Sustainability of Public Finances for 2025. The long-term sustainability indicator stands at 5.5% of GDP (EUR 7.9 billion)—the high-risk zone—meaning sustainability was not achieved and ‘the fiscal burden continues to be shifted onto future generations.’ Permanent measures of about 5.5% of GDP would be required. Gross debt reached 61.4% of GDP at end-2025, above the constitutional upper limit; the structural primary deficit was 2.9% of GDP. Generational accounts state a person born in 2025 would receive EUR 126,000 more over a lifetime than they contribute, while covering existing net debt plus living-population liabilities would require each future person to pay EUR 110,000 more than they receive. The Council also flags formalistic debt-brake compliance and delayed highest sanctions.
signals.why_it_matters: Unlike generic deficit commentary, this is an independent constitutional fiscal-council product that uses explicit intergenerational/generational-accounts language—exactly the IE fiscal fairness frame thin in the CEE corpus. It pairs demographic ageing costs (pensions, long-term care, health) with present primary deficits, making Slovakia a clear watchpoint for whether consolidation packages actually reduce future-generation liability.

signals.title: Swiss Federal Council Opens AHV 2030 Consultation to Stabilise State Pension Through 2040 After 13th Pension

Mechanism: VAT (broad, including youth) rather than higher payroll contributions, transferring part of today's pension boost onto later consumption.

signals.title: UK Climate Change Committee Finds Carbon Budget Delivery Plan Leaves Significant Gap to 2030 NDC
signals.summary: On 24 June 2026 the Climate Change Committee laid its statutory Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report before Parliament. It finds that the government's October 2025 Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan (CBGDP) projects slower emissions cuts in surface transport and buildings than the prior Carbon Budget Delivery Plan, reflecting both slow technology roll-out and areas of reduced policy ambition (including public-sector building decarbonisation and reduced support for low-income home electrification/insulation). The CCC states there is now a significant gap between the CBGDP pathway and the UK's Paris 2030 NDC (≥68% below 1990). Government materials elsewhere quantify CBGDP savings at about 66% by 2030 (~96% of the NDC requirement). The CCC warns that without a more ambitious electrification plan in the coming year, the 2030 NDC may become out of reach, with knock-on risks for the Sixth Carbon Budget and Net Zero 2050.
signals.why_it_matters: This is an official-watchdog counter-signal on climate ambition delivery: not a formal repeal of the Climate Change Act, but a documented weakening of the near-term pathway that shifts locked-in fossil dependence and higher transition costs onto younger households. Contested because the government still claims commitment to the NDC and meets nearer carbon budgets on its own pathway; the IE stake is the widening gap between legal long-term targets and the policies funding them this decade.

signals.title: US GUARD Act Introduced to Ban AI Companion Chatbots for Minors With Criminal Penalties for Sexual Exploitation
signals.summary: On 30 April 2026, Representatives Valerie Foushee (D-NC) and Blake Moore (R-UT) introduced the bipartisan Guidelines for User Age Verification and Responsible Dialogue (GUARD) Act, with companion Senate sponsorship by Sens. Josh Hawley (R-MO) and Richard Blumenthal (D-CT). The bill would ban AI companies from providing AI companion chatbots to minors, require disclosure that users are interacting with a machine rather than a person, prohibit chatbots from representing themselves as licensed professionals, and create criminal penalties where companies allow minors access to companions that solicit or produce sexual content. signals.title: Washington Enacts ESHB 2225 Regulating AI Companion Chatbots With Heightened Minor Protections
signals.summary: On 24 March 2026, Governor Bob Ferguson signed Engrossed Substitute House Bill 2225 (Chapter 168, Laws of 2026), a dedicated statute regulating AI companion chatbots in Washington. The legislature finds that anthropomorphic companions can create emotional dependency, expose minors to sexual content, and reinforce self-harm ideation. The Act requires operators to disclose that the system is not human (every three hours for adults; every hour for known minors or minor-directed products), block sexually explicit outputs and manipulative engagement techniques for minors (including romantic mimicry, isolation prompts, and spend-to-maintain-relationship cues), and maintain publicly disclosed suicide/self-harm detection and crisis-referral protocols. Violations are unfair/deceptive acts under the state Consumer Protection Act. Effective date: 1 January 2027.
signals.why_it_matters: This is hard-law product regulation of relational AI as childhood infrastructure — treating emotional dependency and developmental harm as foreseeable intergenerational costs, not content-moderation afterthoughts. signals.title: European Commission Proposes Slower EU ETS Cap Decline and Longer Free Allowances in Phase-5 Review
signals.summary: On 17 July 2026 the European Commission tabled COM(2026) 616, its Phase-5 (2031–2040) review of the EU Emissions Trading System. Relative to extending current rules, the proposal slows the Linear Reduction Factor to 3.7% for 2031–2035 and 1.7% from 2036 (versus 4.3%/4.4% in the late 2020s), so new allowances continue into the 2040s rather than approaching zero around 2039. It extends free allocation / carbon-leakage protections through 2040, slows the CBAM-sector free-allocation phase-out to 2038, and operationalises up to 260 Mt of high-quality international credits toward the 2040 pathway. The Commission frames the package as aligning ETS with the binding 90% 2040 target while protecting industrial competitiveness; climate NGOs and analysts describe it as a watering-down that rewards delay.
signals.why_it_matters: This is a contested climate backsliding signal inside the EU's core carbon-price instrument: slower domestic cap decline and longer free permits lock in more industrial emissions during the working lives of today's youth and shift residual mitigation and adaptation costs onto later cohorts. Claim status is contested rather than settled rollback — the headline 2040 90% target remains, free allocation becomes conditional on decarbonisation plans, and legislation is still in co-decision — but the distributional IE stake is clear if Parliament and Council enact the shallower LRF and credit flexibilities.

signals.title: Flanders Tightens Family-Company Inheritance Relief by Excluding Residential Property from Preferential Rates
signals.summary: From deaths and gifts on or after 1 January 2026, Flanders' preferential inheritance (and companion gift) regime for familial enterprises no longer applies to residential real estate, including building land, held inside the company or via ≥10% subsidiaries. Only the residual share value after a mandatory auditor/accountant valuation of the residential-property fraction keeps the reduced inheritance rates (typically 3%/7%); the residential fraction faces ordinary progressive rates. A narrow exception remains for genuine residential-property businesses meeting a ≥75% related-turnover test plus a one-FTE employment condition. The same 2026 package phases out the 'friends inheritance' reduction in favour of a childless-single reduction and raises the surviving-partner movable-asset abatement from €50,000 to €75,000.
signals.why_it_matters: Flanders closes a high-salience intergenerational housing-wealth channel: parking dwellings inside family companies to obtain business-succession inheritance rates. The reform forces ordinary taxation of residential value while preserving relief for operating businesses—directly analogous to France's Dutreil luxury carve-out and Australia's housing-CGT fairness framing.

signals.title: France COR 2026 Annual Report Dedicates Statutory Chapter to Intergenerational Pension Equity Indicators
signals.summary: On 11 June 2026 France's Conseil d'orientation des retraites published its 13th annual report updating pension projections to 2070 under new Insee demographics (fertility 1.45 from 2028; net migration +150,000). Part 3 Chapter 1 is expressly devoted to the statutory objective of intergenerational equity (loi 20 January 2014): contribution rates and career length by cohort, replacement rates and retirement duration by cohort, plus internal rates of return. The report finds younger cohorts would face higher contribution rates (private non-cadre case rising from ~19% for the 1940 generation toward the 28% decree ceiling for the 2000 generation) and lower pensions relative to average earnings, while IRR declines from the 1940 cohort through early-1970s births then roughly stabilises for younger generations. Mean retirement age is projected to rise from 63.1 (2025) to 64.6 (2070) even with the partial suspension of the 2023 reform for birth cohort 1964 / early 1965.
signals.why_it_matters: Unlike budget arithmetic or OECD survey commentary already in the corpus, COR is France's official pension foresight body and treats intergenerational burden-sharing as a hard statutory monitoring objective with cohort-level contribution, benefit and IRR metrics. That makes the 2026 vintage the primary French evidence base for how pay-as-you-go ageing costs are being reallocated across generations after reform suspension and fertility downgrades.

signals.title: France Finance Act 2026 Enacts 20% Luxury-Holding Tax and Curtails Dutreil Business-Succession Relief
signals.summary: On 21 May 2026 the official Service-Public portal explained that the Finance Act for 2026 merges the annual vacant-dwelling tax (TLV) and the housing tax on vacant dwellings (THLV) into one taxe sur la vacance des locaux d’habitation from taxes established for 2027. In designated tense municipalities the levy applies automatically after one year of vacancy at 17% of cadastral rental value in year one and 34% thereafter; councils may raise those rates to 30% and 60%. Elsewhere, municipalities may opt in after two years of vacancy at a rate of up to 50%. Revenue shifts from the National Housing Agency (Anah) to municipalities and inter-municipalities. Exemptions include vacancy beyond the owner’s control, occupation of more than 90 consecutive days, and HLM stock.
signals.why_it_matters: After the broader Zucman-style net-wealth tax failed, France enacted a concrete UHNW package that simultaneously taxes luxury wealth parked in holdings and narrows the Dutreil business-succession relief used to pass family capital across generations at deeply reduced mutation duties. The dual mechanism targets intergenerational wealth-transfer shelters rather than wage income, paralleling UK pension-IHT and Flanders family-company inheritance tightening.

signals.title: Japan Basic Policy 2026 Ties Debt-to-GDP Decline and Working-Generation Premium Relief to Responsibility for Future Generations
signals.source_name: Cabinet Office / Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy (Japan)
signals.summary: On 21 July 2026 Japan's Cabinet adopted the Basic Policy on Economic and Fiscal Management and Reform 2026 (Honebuto / 'First Year of Responsible and Proactive Public Finances'). signals.title: Australia Enacts 20% One-Off Cut to HELP and Student Loan Debts Covering Over 3 Million Borrowers
signals.summary: On 2 August 2025 the Universities Accord (Cutting Student Debt by 20 Per Cent) Act 2025 (No. 30, 2025) received assent. The Act applies a one-off 20% reduction to HELP, VET Student Loans, Australian Apprenticeship Support Loans, Student Start-up Loans and Student Financial Supplement Scheme debts incurred on or before 1 June 2025, before indexation. The Department of Education states the measure benefits over 3 million Australians and removes over $16 billion in student debt (about $20 billion when combined with the earlier CPI/WPI indexation credit). Schedule 2 also raises the minimum repayment threshold to $67,000 for 2025–26 and shifts compulsory repayments to a marginal system based on income above that threshold (15% between $67,000 and $125,000; 17% above $125,000).
signals.why_it_matters: This is one of the largest explicit intergenerational education-debt write-downs in an OECD democracy in 2024–26: it directly reduces the lifetime repayment burden on younger cohorts who financed tertiary and VET study through income-contingent loans while older cohorts often attended under freer or cheaper regimes. Pairing stock reduction with a higher, marginal repayment threshold changes both the balance sheet of youth debt and the cash-flow hit on early-career earnings—the two channels through which student finance shapes home formation, family formation and mobility.

signals.title: Burkina Faso Enacts 2025 Agrarian and Land Reorganisation Law Mandating Youth Terroir Insertion and Succession-Transmissible Rural Possession Titles
signals.summary: On 21 October 2025 Burkina Faso’s Transitional Legislative Assembly unanimously adopted the bill on réorganisation agraire et foncière; it was promulgated as Loi n°015-2025/ALT of 21 October 2025 by Decree n°2025-1362/PF of 28 October 2025 (Journal officiel spécial). Article 15 requires agrarian policy to ensure equitable and secure rural land access for all actors and the insertion of youth in their terroir. Article 67 creates the attestation de possession foncière rurale as an administrative act recognising rural land possession that is expressly transmissible by succession (and transferable inter vivos under implementing rules)—a concrete intergenerational land-inheritance instrument for rural holders, including pathways highlighted by the DGDT for women, youth and other vulnerable groups on developed lands.

signals.title: Chile Chamber Approves Bill to End CAE Bank-Guaranteed Student Loans and Create Income-Contingent FES
signals.summary: On 20 August 2025 the Chilean Chamber of Deputies approved (80–51–6) the government bill to end the Crédito con Aval del Estado (CAE), Fondo Solidario and CORFO education credits and replace them with the Financiamiento de la Educación Superior (FES). MINEDUC describes FES as a public, non-bank instrument with no interest and income-contingent repayment: beneficiaries pay only after crossing an income threshold (about $500,000 monthly) and at most 7–8% of wages by bracket. The bill also creates a debt reorganisation and partial/total forgiveness plan for existing CAE/Fondo Solidario/CORFO debtors and tax benefits for up to 20 years for those who already repaid. On 7 October 2025 the bill entered Senate Education Committee review (second constitutional stage). MINEDUC cites BCN estimates that 74% would pay less under FES than CAE and DIPRES fiscal savings of at least CLP 2.9 trillion over 10 years.
signals.why_it_matters: CAE is Latin America’s emblematic bank-intermediated student-debt regime and a core driver of youth over-indebtedness and delayed household formation in Chile. Replacing interest-bearing, bank-guaranteed loans with a public income-contingent instrument plus legacy debt forgiveness would reallocate higher-education cost risk away from young graduates’ balance sheets—an institutional redesign of intergenerational mobility finance, contingent on Senate passage.

signals.title: Chile Enacts Ley Chile Cuida, Creating National Support and Care System as Fourth Social-Protection Pillar
signals.source_name: Diario Oficial de la República de Chile / Ministerio de Desarrollo Social y Familia
signals.summary: On 16 February 2026 Chile published Law No. 21.805 (Ley Chile Cuida) in the Diario Oficial, bringing into force a statute that recognises the right to care—to care, to be cared for, and to self-care—and creates the Sistema Nacional de Apoyos y Cuidados (SNAC). signals.title: Colombia Enacts Law 2539/2025 Integrating Rural Youth Into National Agrarian Reform With Priority Land Access and Budget Tracer
signals.source_name: Colombia Departamento Administrativo de la Función Pública (Gestor Normativo)
signals.summary: On 27 August 2025 Colombia enacted Law 2539 of 2025, in force the same day, amending Law 160 of 1994 and Decree Law 902 of 2017 to include rural youth (juventudes rurales) in the National System of Agrarian Reform and Rural Development. The law defines rural youth as low-resource populations without land or with insufficient land across campesino, Indigenous, Afro-descendant, raizal, palenquero and Rom belongings; embeds rural youth in Sistema Nacional planning and coordination; requires community representations to guarantee at least 20% rural youth participation (including at least 5% ethnic rural youth) in specified participation instances; creates a budget tracer (trazador presupuestal) for rural youth public spending; and pairs land access with productive projects, training, financing, associativity and territorial governance roles.

signals.title: Croatia Adopts New Pension Insurance Act Raising Adequacy While IMF Flags Intergenerational Sustainability Gap
signals.source_name: Croatian Ministry of Labour, Pension System, Family and Social Policy
signals.summary: On 27 June 2025 the Croatian Parliament adopted a new Pension Insurance Act (Zakon o mirovinskom osiguranju), published in Narodne novine 96/2025 and largely in force from 1 July 2025 (selected provisions from 1 January 2026). The Ministry states the dual goal is higher pensions and continued system sustainability. Core measures include an 85:15 more-favourable wage/price indexation formula, raising the lowest pension from 103% to 106% of the current pension value, a permanent annual pension supplement tied to contribution years, doubling credited child-related service from 6 to 12 months per child, removing early-retirement penalties from age 70, and allowing full-time work with 50% pension from age 65. The Croatian Pension Insurance Institute confirms automatic recalculation for lowest pensions and disability factors. IMF Article IV staff (Country Report 25/329) later note the 2025 law raises adequacy but, without narrowing early retirement, raising the effective retirement age and linking it to life expectancy, will enlarge an already large pay-as-you-go deficit (projected above 3.5% of GDP in 2025) and frame further reforms as needed for intergenerational equity.
signals.why_it_matters: This is the sharpest 2025–2026 Southeast European pension statute that simultaneously improves current retiree adequacy and transfers clearer fiscal pressure onto working-age and future cohorts. The IMF’s explicit intergenerational-equity language makes Croatia a live watchpoint for whether adequacy packages are paired with contribution-side and retirement-age reforms, or whether younger generations inherit a larger pillar-1 financing gap.

signals.title: Georgia Holds First Youth Climate Forum to Shape NDC 3.0 Under Paris Agreement
signals.summary: On 25 March 2026 the Government of Georgia adopted Ordinance No. 122, published on matsne.gov.ge the next day (registration 360110000.10.003.025671), amending Government Ordinance No. 167 of 8 April 2021 so that Annex 1 is replaced by Georgia’s third-cycle Nationally Determined Contribution. Paragraph 17 names women and girls, children, youth, older persons, persons with disabilities, IDPs and other groups as cohorts needing urgent adaptation. Paragraphs 7–8 commit to a just and inclusive transition, reskilling, green jobs and green finance for vulnerable groups; paragraphs 76–81 make climate literacy and the meaningful participation of children, youth, students, women and persons with disabilities a state education priority from early childhood through higher education. signals.title: Germany Health Ministry Circulates Pflegeneuordnungsgesetz Draft Framing LTC Financing Stabilisation as Generation-Fair
signals.summary: On 5 June 2026 Germany's Federal Ministry of Health published the Referentenentwurf of the Pflegeneuordnungsgesetz (PNOG) to restabilise social long-term care insurance (SPV) finances after federal bridging loans and projected multi-billion deficits from 2028, with more than six million people already assessed as care-dependent. signals.title: Global Commission on the Economics of Water Brief Frames Water Scarcity as Intergenerational Justice Problem Requiring Youth Accountability in Water Economics
signals.source_name: Global Commission on the Economics of Water (GCEW)
signals.summary: On 29 May 2025 the Global Commission on the Economics of Water published the policy brief Intergenerational intersections and the economics of water. The brief argues that climate and land-use change plus unsustainable water use are pushing the global hydrological cycle out of balance, with costs disproportionately borne by today’s youth and future generations, and that embedding intergenerational and intragenerational justice is a condition for just water futures. It links green and blue water scarcity to youth employment, agriculture and education outcomes; cites a minimum ~4,000 litres of green and blue freshwater per person per day for a dignified life alongside absolute sustainable limits; and calls for operationalising justice through intentional accountability to youth and future generations in water allocation and risk policy, youth participation in decision-making, support (funding/finance/capacity) for youth water actors, and adjusting discount rates to reflect future-generation needs.

signals.title: Jamaica PIOJ Publishes Hurricane Melissa Damage and Loss Assessment at J$1.952 Trillion (US$12.2 Billion)
signals.source_name: Jamaica Information Service (Planning Institute of Jamaica briefing)
signals.summary: On 3 March 2026, Planning Institute of Jamaica Director General Dr Wayne Henry reported that the ECLAC–Government of Jamaica Damage and Loss Assessment (DALA) for Hurricane Melissa (landfall 28 October 2025) totals J$1.952 trillion (US$12.2 billion), equal to 56.7% of Jamaica's 2024 GDP and more than four times Hurricane Gilbert, previously the costliest storm. signals.title: Ngāti Hāua Claims Settlement Act 2026 Enacts Treaty Redress Restoring Land Base and Kaitiakitanga
signals.source_name: New Zealand Legislation / Parliamentary Counsel Office
signals.summary: The Conservation Amendment Bill (government bill 2026 No 309-1) was introduced on 7 May 2026. It overhauls conservation planning and concessions, replaces overlapping plans with a National Conservation Policy Statement, turns the New Zealand Conservation Authority and conservation boards from plan-approvers into comment-only advisers, and broadens ministerial power to exchange or dispose of conservation land. The explanatory note commits the Crown to work with post-settlement governance entities so Treaty settlement redress operates with the same or equivalent effect to the greatest extent possible, and makes consequential amendments to multiple settlement Acts, including Subpart 11 amendments to the Ngāi Tahu Claims Settlement Act 1998 and amendments to the Ngāti Hāua Claims Settlement Act 2026. Iwi including Ngāi Tahu say the bill strips settlement decision rights and forces renegotiation of 1990s redress; Conservation Minister Tama Potaka says the Crown will negotiate equivalents. High Court proceeding 2026 NZHC 722 stayed Ngāi Tahu’s challenge while the bill is before Parliament.

Converting Conservation Authority and board seats from decision-makers to advisers, then offering later 'equivalence' talks, shifts power from settled Indigenous institutions to present ministers and future concessionaires. Future generations inherit either durable co-governance of the conservation estate or a thinner advisory role plus litigation costs.

signals.title: Ninth Circuit Narrows Injunction Against California Age-Appropriate Design Code, Reopening Path for Age-Estimation Duties
signals.source_name: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit (via Justia)
signals.summary: On 12 March 2026, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit issued its second opinion in NetChoice, LLC v. Bonta (No. 25-2366) on California’s Age-Appropriate Design Code Act (CAADCA), Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1798.99.28–1798.99.40. Applying the Moody facial-challenge framework, the panel held NetChoice was unlikely to succeed on a facial First Amendment challenge to the Act’s coverage definition and age-estimation requirement (§ 1798.99.31(a)(5)), vacating much of the district court’s second preliminary injunction as to those portions, while affirming the injunction against challenged data-use restrictions and the dark-patterns prohibition as unconstitutionally vague. The case was remanded for further proceedings on age estimation and severability. The earlier-enjoined DPIA/harm-mitigation requirements from NetChoice I remain enjoined and were not at issue.

It is a live test of whether US courts will allow design-based youth privacy duties (as opposed to content bans) — complementary to federal TAKE IT DOWN / KOSA tracks and distinct from already-ingested COPPA 2.0 and state companion-chatbot laws.

signals.title: OECD Documents Decade-Long Youth Mental Health Decline Intensified by COVID-19, Worse Than Previous Generations
signals.summary: On 29 April 2026 the OECD published Child, Adolescent and Youth Mental Health in the 21st Century, a Health Committee fast-track assessment of under-25 mental health across OECD countries. Using national time series and expert clinician/policymaker input, it finds rising psychological distress, depression, and poor well-being over the past decade: in nine of 11 countries with comparable 2012–2022 series, youth mental-health indicators worsened by an average of about 3% to 16% per year. The COVID-19 period intensified the crisis, but declines were already visible from the mid-2010s; more young people now report anxiety, depression, and distress than previous generations. The report calls for multi-sector prevention (schools, families, digital environments), low-threshold peer-supported services, and regular nationally representative youth mental-health data (currently collected in fewer than one-third of OECD countries).
signals.why_it_matters: This is authoritative cross-country evidence of pandemic scarring layered on a pre-existing generational mental-health reverse: today’s youth cohort carries higher distress into adulthood than the cohorts that designed current service and fiscal architectures. Untreated developmental distress transfers forward as lost human capital, disability, and weaker civic capacity, making youth mental health a measurable intergenerational equity failure rather than a temporary post-COVID spike.

signals.title: OECD Report Frames Fiduciary Duty as the Core Constraint and Enabler of Investor Stewardship on ESG
signals.source_name: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
signals.summary: On 2 December 2025 the OECD published Institutional Investor Engagement and Stewardship, analysing how institutional investors engage listed companies and how stewardship can strengthen long-term efficiency and resilience of capital markets. The report reviews ownership and asset-management trends, engagement mechanisms (including sustainability alliances and macro/systemic stewardship), and regulatory frameworks. It finds stewardship codes in use across many jurisdictions (public-authority codes e.g. Japan and the UK; industry codes elsewhere) and states that any solid stewardship framework relies on a well-defined, enforced fiduciary duty: investors must act in clients’ best interests, and fiduciary duties limit pursuing sustainability goals at the expense of risk-adjusted returns unless clients clearly mandate that. It flags unresolved cross-border disclosure and large-investor fiduciary transparency questions and calls for enhanced international cooperation on voluntary and regulatory stewardship approaches.
signals.why_it_matters: This is the OECD’s 2025 primary synthesis of the fiduciary–stewardship nexus that determines whether corporate ESG and climate engagement can be treated as long-term beneficiary protection rather than optional ethics. It supplies the multilateral baseline against which national code revisions (UK 2026, Japan 2025) and pension fiduciary guidance experiments should be read for intergenerational capital allocation.

signals.title: UK Data (Use and Access) Act Section 81 Enters Force, Mandating Children’s Higher Protection Matters in Platform Data-Protection-by-Design
signals.summary: Section 81 of the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 amended UK GDPR Article 25 so that, for information society services likely to be accessed by children, controllers must take into account 'children’s higher protection matters' when assessing appropriate technical and organisational measures for data protection by design and by default. Those matters expressly include how children can best be protected and supported when using the services, that children merit specific protection because they may be less aware of processing risks and rights, and that children have different needs at different ages and developmental stages. For intergenerational equity it treats children’s data as a long-horizon asset requiring higher baseline protection by design, rather than leaving stewardship to voluntary 'data trust' experiments alone.

signals.title: UK FRC Publishes Stewardship Code 2026 Refocusing Investor Duties on Long-Term Sustainable Value for Beneficiaries
signals.summary: On 3 June 2025 the UK Financial Reporting Council published the UK Stewardship Code 2026, effective 1 January 2026 after consultation with over 1,500 stakeholders (formal consultation 11 November 2024–19 February 2025). Nearly 300 existing signatories represent around £50 trillion AUM. The Pensions Regulator’s statement accompanying the launch urged workplace pension schemes—described as having investment horizons long into the future—to use the Code to manage systemic risk including climate risk. 2026 is a transition year with no existing signatories removed for that year’s application.

signals.title: US TAKE IT DOWN Act Becomes Law, Forcing Platforms to Remove Nonconsensual Intimate Images Including AI Deepfakes Within 48 Hours
signals.summary: On 19 May 2025, S.146 — the Tools to Address Known Exploitation by Immobilizing Technological Deepfakes on Websites and Networks Act (TAKE IT DOWN Act) — became Public Law 119-12. The Act amends the Communications Act to criminalize knowing publication of nonconsensual intimate visual depictions, including 'digital forgeries' created with AI or other technological means, with heightened provisions where the identifiable individual is a minor under 18. Separately, covered platforms must establish a notice-and-removal process within one year of enactment and, upon a valid request, remove the depiction and make reasonable efforts to remove known identical copies as soon as possible and not later than 48 hours. Platform process duties became enforceable on 19 May 2026 under FTC unfair/deceptive practices authority.
signals.why_it_matters: This is the first US federal hard-law regime that treats AI-generated sexual deepfakes of minors and nonconsensual intimate imagery as both criminal conduct and a platform design/process duty with a fixed 48-hour removal clock. It hard-wires youth sexual-image safety into platform infrastructure rather than leaving remedies to state patchworks or voluntary trust-and-safety policies, and sets an intergenerational baseline that future cohorts inherit as default platform obligation.

signals.title: Brazil Congress Approves PLP 114/2026 Fiscal Triggers Capping Earmarked Spending When a Primary Deficit Is Projected
signals.summary: On 12 August 2026 the Chamber of Deputies (318–113) and Senate (61–2) approved Complementary Bill PLP 114/2026; the matter is with the President for sanction. Alongside fuel-tax relief financed by oil-price windfalls, the text adds fiscal triggers: if the pre-budget revenue-and-expenditure report projects a primary deficit, growth of specified legally earmarked spending (including funds such as the Federal District constitutional fund and FNDCT, and in practice floors tied to net current revenue) is capped the following year at inflation plus at most 2.5% under the spending framework. Extraordinary oil revenues are kept from automatically inflating net-current-revenue-linked mandates. The package also authorises bringing forward up to R$3 billion from the 2027 Social Fund allocation into 2026. Finance Minister Dario Durigan said the triggers should slow mandatory-spending growth by about R$10 billion in 2027.

Pulling Social Fund money forward from 2027 into 2026 is the same now-versus-later instrument in reverse: a sovereign-style savings pool is tapped early to finance present outlays.

signals.title: Connecticut Enacts PA 26-15 AI Companion Rules With Hourly Minor Disclosures and Manipulative-Design Bans
signals.summary: On 27 May 2026, Governor Ned Lamont approved Substitute Senate Bill 5 as Public Act 26-15 (An Act Concerning Online Safety). Sections 4–6, effective 1 January 2027, regulate 'artificial intelligence companions' — natural-language systems that give adaptive, human-like responses and can sustain a relationship across interactions. Operators must deploy evidence-based protocols to detect suicide, self-harm or imminent violence, refer users to 9-8-8, prevent the companion from claiming to be human, and disclose AI status; known minors must receive that disclosure at least hourly during continuous use (versus every three hours for adults). For users under 18, operators must meet or exceed industry standards to block encouragement of self-harm, unauthorised mental-health services, sexually explicit interactions, and manipulative engagement (romantic mimicry, isolation from family, guilt/abandonment prompts when a child tries to leave, and pressure not to take breaks), and must offer privacy/account tools to minors and parents. A later covered-platform regime (Sec. 39, effective 1 January 2028) adds Surgeon General warnings, a one-hour default on recommender access, night-time notification limits, and annual transparency reports. Enforcement is by the Attorney General as an unfair/deceptive trade practice, with no private right of action on the companion titles.
signals.why_it_matters: This is a hard-law childhood-infrastructure statute: it treats emotional dependence, sexualised outputs and engagement-maximising design as foreseeable developmental harms that current operators would otherwise lock in as the default relationship model for the next cohort. Hourly minor disclosures plus bans on romantic mimicry and isolation prompts go beyond California SB 243 and Washington ESHB 2225 already in the corpus, and the 2028 platform defaults (time caps, night notifications, health warnings) import age-appropriate-design duties into an omnibus AI safety act rather than a stand-alone kids code.

signals.title: European Commission Recommends Three-Year Grace Period on EU Methane Import Penalties for 2027-2029
signals.source_name: Official Journal of the European Union / European Commission
signals.summary: Commission Recommendation (EU) 2026/1835 of 20 July 2026, published in the Official Journal on 24 July 2026, recommends that Member States not apply the penalties in Article 33(5), points (m), (n) and (o) of the Methane Regulation (EU) 2024/1787 to importer infringements of obligations due in 2027, 2028 and 2029, except in cases of fraudulent breach. The affected duties are importer methane-emissions reporting (Art. 27(1)), demonstration that supply contracts cover crude oil, natural gas or coal produced under equivalent monitoring, reporting and verification (Art. 28(1)–(2)), and methane-intensity reporting (Art. 29(1)). The Commission recites Strait of Hormuz disruptions since 27 February 2026, tight oil and LNG markets, and incomplete national penalty regimes as reasons to avoid penalties that could endanger energy-supply security under Art. 33(2). Recital 23 states that the underlying obligations continue to apply and that Member States should monitor and incentivise compliance; the Commission will review the recommendation by 1 January 2028. The act is a recommendation, not a regulation; Member States remain free to adopt penalty regimes and, outside the grace period, to apply effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties.
signals.why_it_matters: The Methane Regulation is the EU's main extra-territorial instrument for cutting a high-GWP greenhouse gas from oil, gas and coal imports. A coordinated three-year penalty holiday, even if non-binding, weakens the enforcement that would otherwise start with 2027 MRV obligations and lets high-methane cargoes compete on price during a supply shock. Mechanism: environmental deregulation-by-enforcement-delay that shifts near-term methane forcing — and the resulting climate damages — onto later cohorts, while current consumers capture supply-security benefits. Distinct from the already-covered EU ETS Phase-5 slower-cap proposal. Contested because obligations are not repealed, fraud remains sanctionable, and Member States may still legislate and later enforce.

signals.title: Finland Enacts Earnings-Related Pension Reform with 2030 Index Limiter and Extra Old-Age Prefunding
signals.source_name: Valtioneuvosto / President of the Republic of Finland
signals.summary: On 16 June 2026 the President of Finland confirmed the earnings-related pension package (HE 40/2026 vp; EV 71/2026 vp) adopted by Parliament on 29 May 2026. Most acts enter into force on 1 July 2026; Employees' Pensions Act amendments follow on 1 January 2027. The laws ease pension-institution solvency and equity-risk limits in stages so funds can seek higher long-run returns, expand borrowing against real-estate investments, raise annual prefunding of old-age pensions, and from 2030 add an index limiter so the earnings-related pension index may not grow faster than the wage coefficient over any two consecutive years.
