signals.title: Norway’s DFØ Guidance Now Requires Child-Impact Analysis in Pre-Decision Appraisals of State Measures
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: The revised Instructions for Official Studies (utredningsinstruksen), adopted by Royal Decree on 18 October 2024 and in force from 1 November 2024, govern how Norwegian ministries and agencies must appraise state measures before decision. DFØ’s accompanying guide — updated with the revision — now states that when a measure has direct or indirect significance for children, the appraisal 'shall' assess what effects it will have for children so that the best interests of the child are safeguarded. Children are also listed among groups that can raise 'principled questions' under minimum question 3 (alongside Indigenous peoples and minorities). The Children’s Ombudsperson (25 October 2024) treated the new guide as requiring decision-makers to assess consequences for children, hear children and young people, and take a view on the child’s best interests before introducing new measures. The guide is not itself a statute; the Instructions bind the state administration. No 2025–26 law creating a standalone CRIA was found.
signals.why_it_matters: The IIA mechanism is a cross-government pre-decision appraisal duty: ministries must identify who is affected and, where children are affected, assess child impacts and best interests before reforms, regulations or investments are adopted. Legal force is an administrative instruction plus official guidance, not a CRWIA-style statute, but it applies to state measures generally rather than only child-titled bills. signals.title: OECD Youth Policy Toolkit Instructs Governments to Run Youth-Check RIAs and Embed Intergenerational Perspectives in Rulemaking
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: On 26 November 2024 the OECD launched the Youth Policy Toolkit to operationalise the 2022 Council Recommendation on Creating Better Opportunities for Young People. The toolkit's public-governance pillar (Recommendation VI.3) tells governments to embed an intergenerational perspective in rulemaking, budgeting, procurement and infrastructure so present decisions do not compromise future generations. It instructs officials to systematically apply regulatory impact assessments and strategic foresight to age-group and future-generation inequalities, and documents live youth-check models: Austria's Child and Youth Impact Assessment on all new legislative proposals for ages 0-30 (since 2013); Flanders' JoKER child-and-youth report inside RIA for ages 0-25 (since 2008); France's Youth Impact Clause covering youth, intergenerational justice and non-discrimination (since 2009); Germany's Competence Centre Youth-Check, which examined 543 draft bills and published 126 youth-checks between 2017 and 2021; and Parma's January 2024 municipal generational impact evaluation with published guidelines, indicators and participation steps. The toolkit also records the European Commission's 2024 commitment to apply a youth check through Better Regulation tools.
signals.why_it_matters: This is the closest OECD-issued operating manual for Intergenerational Impact Assessment cousins. Mechanism: before a law or regulation is adopted, a named youth-check or RIA step must assess effects on children, young people and (in the French clause) intergenerational justice, using age-disaggregated evidence; legal force ranges from integration inside national RIA systems to a dedicated competence centre. It is not a single binding IIA standard, but it is the first OECD compilation that tells administrations which steps, age bands and institutional owners to copy.

signals.title: Statistics Norway Publishes 2026 Technical Documentation of the Ministry-Commissioned Generational Accounts Model
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: On 24 February 2026 SSB published Notater 2026/7, Generasjonsregnskapet — technical documentation of the generational-accounts model it built for the Ministry of Finance from 2007. The model computes present-value net taxes and transfers by age-sex cohort and a generation equation for long-run fiscal imbalance. The preface states it was used in the National Budget from 2008 through 2013, has not been used in ordinary budget work since, and still rests on that-era data. The 2026 note exists because internal documentation was completed 'in connection with work on a new framework for public finances in the long term' (et nytt rammeverk for offentlige finanser på lang sikt). A companion MAKKO municipal-economy module feeds age-sex public-consumption paths into the generation equation.

The 2026 publication is a methods revival inside a new long-term public-finance framework, not a return of the test to Prinsjesdag-style budget papers. Mechanism: SSB/MoF generational accounts as a potential budget IA that is documented and production-ready (DAPLA) yet currently unused at the budget gate.

signals.title: Swedish NIER 2026 Fiscal Sustainability Report Tests Whether Future Generations Face Today's Welfare Bargain
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: On 4 March 2026 Konjunkturinstitutet, a government agency under the Ministry of Finance with a statutory mandate in Act (2007:759), published Fiscal Sustainability Report 2026 (Specialstudie 124). The baseline holds today's tax rules, transfer replacement rates and public-service staffing constant to 2060 and asks whether future generations would still face a welfare system and financing structure broadly similar to today's — the report cites generational accounts (ESO 1995) as the standard approach. NIER judges the baseline sustainable because net financial worth and Maastricht debt do not deteriorate persistently, while stating that a weakening net position 'implies that expenditures are shifted to future generations.' Defence-build-up scenarios to NATO's 3.5% of GDP show that borrowing the increase without budget-strengthening measures keeps net lending negative and the net position on a declining path.
signals.why_it_matters: Sweden's official long-term fiscal test is an OBR-style sustainability IIA with an explicit future-generation incidence rule: NIER must tell the government whether current policy can be continued so later cohorts inherit the same welfare/tax bargain, and it treats rising debt as a transfer onto those cohorts. Mechanism: statutory annual sustainability report to the Ministry of Finance, not a line-by-line Budget IA, but it is the document that scores whether today's fiscal stance fails future generations. Not in the corpus.

policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: In 2025 UNICEF published the Digital Child Rights Impact Assessment (D-CRIA) Toolbox for companies developing, deploying or using digital technologies including AI. signals.title: Wales Makes Long-Term Health Impact Assessments Mandatory for Strategic Public Decisions from April 2027
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: The Health Impact Assessment (Wales) Regulations 2025 (WSI 2025/1215 (W. 198)) were made on 19 November 2025 after Senedd approval and come into force on 6 April 2027. They commence the unused Part 6 power in the Public Health (Wales) Act 2017. Regulation 3 requires listed public bodies to carry out a health impact assessment when proposing a decision of a strategic nature about how to exercise their functions. A HIA is defined as an assessment of likely short- and long-term effects on the physical and mental health of the people of Wales or some of them. Regulation 4 requires the body to identify affected population groups, intended and likely unintended health effects, mitigation or enhancement measures, and to have regard to wider social, economic, cultural and environmental determinants of health and to health inequity factors (including socio-economic status, geography and Equality Act protected characteristics). Regulation 6 requires publication of the HIA as soon as reasonably practicable. Regulation 7 adds further public bodies, including corporate joint committees, Transport for Wales, Social Care Wales and the Welsh Revenue Authority. The Cabinet Secretary's 25 November 2025 written statement says the duty covers 56 organisations, including the Welsh Ministers and local authorities, and is intended to support Well-being of Future Generations (Wales) Act 2015 obligations. Welsh Government supporting information states that a public body that fails to comply may be subject to legal challenge.
signals.why_it_matters: This is a 2025–26 statutory instrument that makes a long-horizon wellbeing-style impact assessment legally mandatory before strategic decisions, rather than another retrospective of the 2015 Well-being Act. Mechanism: specified public bodies, including Welsh Ministers and local authorities, must assess short- and long-term physical and mental health effects, including inequity and wider determinants, before a strategic decision, then publish the assessment. Legal force: Welsh statutory instrument under the 2017 Public Health Act, in force 6 April 2027, with potential judicial review for non-compliance. It is the distinct IIA-cousin regulation the Wales hunt asked for, sitting beside (not replacing) administrative Integrated Impact Assessments used in budget papers.

signals.title: Welsh 2026-27 Budget SIIA Reports Wellbeing Impact Workshops Informed Allocations but Did Not Remove Disproportionate Harms
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: The Welsh Government's January 2026 Strategic Integrated Impact Assessment (SIIA) for the 2026-27 Final Budget is the official tool used to assess spending against equality, sustainability and the Well-being of Future Generations (Wales) Act 2015. For this cycle the SIIA moved from a single draft-budget paper to an interim assessment plus a final assessment, with cross-portfolio workshops after the Draft Budget. The Final Assessment states that those conversations 'directly informed targeted Final Budget allocations', citing among others £5m resource to protect bus services, £5m for apprenticeships, extra FE participation funding, ALN delivery resource, a £112.8m local-government uplift and homelessness-prevention funding, and presents ALN and school-estate case studies as preventative, evidence-led choices. The same document's 'Spending Decisions with Identified Negative or Disproportionate Impacts' section records that the SIIA did not eliminate harms: rail support may be regressive relative to buses; the local-government uplift 'does not fully resolve structural pressures' so councils may still cut social care, ALN and homelessness services affecting children and young people; and extra FE resource is unlikely to clear Level 1/Entry waiting lists, with NEET risk remaining. Corpus rg found no SIIA signal; Audit Wales 'No time to lose' and Senedd Fit for the Future are separate Act-level reviews.
signals.why_it_matters: This is a rare official self-evaluation of whether a future-generations budget IIA actually changes money. Mechanism: ministers must consider cumulative wellbeing, equality and WFG five-ways-of-working impacts before Final Budget adoption, now in a two-stage SIIA. Outcome: the government claims workshop evidence shaped specific allocations (buses, ALN, FE, apprenticeships) while also documenting residual cuts and regressive risks the SIIA did not reverse. It bites at the margin of additional in-year allocations, not as a veto on structurally harmful baselines — consistent with Audit Wales's finding that the Act has not driven system-wide change.

signals.title: World Bank Ships LTGM-HC Toolkit Projecting Cohort Human Capital from 2025 to 2100 for 153 Countries
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: In October 2025 the World Bank posted LTGM-HC v1.0, an Excel human-capital extension of the Long-Term Growth Model; the accompanying Policy Research Working Paper 11276 by Mendes and Pennings is dated December 2025. The toolkit projects workforce human capital from 2025 to 2100 for 153 countries using the Human Capital Index ingredients (learning-adjusted years of pre-tertiary schooling; adult survival; child not-stunted rates) embedded in age cohorts. Users compare reform scenarios (for example raising secondary completion versus test scores) and feed the resulting human-capital growth path into the standard LTGM to see GDP effects. Without new reforms, average human-capital growth slows about 0.15–0.2 percentage points per decade and hits zero around 2080 when today's children retire; a typical reform path almost halves that decline. About two thirds of projected GDP-per-capita gains to 2100 already come from past reforms.
signals.why_it_matters: This is official World Bank human-capital impact-assessment kit, not a legal IIA. Mechanism: before locking education or health reforms, finance and planning ministries can quantify how today's child cohorts change workforce productivity and growth through 2100, making the intergenerational return of underinvestment visible. It does not replace generational accounting of taxes and transfers (no IMF 2025-26 GA manual was found) and is distinct from the May 2026 HCI+ dashboard already in the corpus.

signals.title: Australian Treasury's 2023 Intergenerational Report Is the Current Statutory 40-Year Fiscal IIA; No 2025-26 Federal IGR Yet
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: On 24 August 2023 the Australian Treasury published Intergenerational Report 2023: Australia's future to 2063, the sixth federal IGR, projecting the economy and Budget to 2062-63. The Treasurer's official publication page and the IGR hub still treat 2023 as the current report as of 17 August 2026; no 2025 or 2026 federal IGR has been released. The report is required by the Charter of Budget Honesty Act 1998 Part 6: section 20 obliges the Treasurer to publicly release and table an IGR at least once every five years, and section 21 requires it to assess the long-term sustainability of current Government policies over the following 40 years, including the financial implications of demographic change. The 2023 edition names five structural forces (ageing, digital transformation, climate/net-zero, care demand, geopolitics) and frames budget repair as reducing the debt burden on future generations.

Mechanism: the Treasurer must publish and table a 40-year no-policy-change assessment of whether today's tax-and-spend settings are sustainable for later cohorts, with legal force from Charter of Budget Honesty Act 1998 ss 20-21 (at least every five years). It is not a bill-level gate and does not stop a law, but it is the Commonwealth's only recurring intergenerational budget test. The instrument was on the AU country page and missing from the signal corpus.

signals.title: Hungary Future Generations Deputy Records Act CXI Opinion Duty Was Skipped on T/3613 Spatial Planning Bill

policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: The Deputy Commissioner for Future Generations issued a parliamentary figyelmeztetés (attention notice) on bill T/3613, which merged the national, Budapest-agglomeration and Lake Balaton spatial plans into one statute (later 2018. évi CXXXIX. törvény, adopted 12 December 2018). The notice states that Act CXI of 2011 makes protection of future generations the Deputy's task, then records that the proposal did not reach AJBH during administrative consultation, so the Deputy could not judge any attached impact-assessment materials. Public annexes contained no environmental assessment of the plan-type instrument even though Government Decree 2/2005 required one. The Deputy warned MPs that dropping zonal plan-sheets from statute, deleting percentage land-use rules, moving Balaton shoreline rehabilitation plans to ministerial decree, simplifying mining-plot approvals, and letting Government set special rules for priority investments would lower the achieved protection level contrary to Article P and Constitutional Court decision 16/2015 (VI. 5.). signals.why_it_matters: Hungary's IIA-cousin is the Act CXI section 2(2) duty to give an opinion on draft laws and plans that directly affect future generations' quality of life, before they proceed. Bite status: skipped. On a named spatial-planning bill the promoting ministry did not send the draft to AJBH in administrative consultation, so the statutory opinion gate never ran ex ante; the Deputy could only warn Parliament after tabling. That is primary-source evidence the duty can be bypassed on an irreversible land-use statute, distinct from the later Constitutional Court climate-target annulment already in the corpus.

signals.title: Netherlands Publishes a Completed Generatietoets on the National Circular Economy Programme 2023-2030
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: On 20 March 2025 the Dutch Senate published a completed Generatietoets (dated 18 December 2024, Sira Consulting) on the Nationaal Programma Circulaire Economie 2023-2030, applied to product-lifetime-extension measures for electronics, furniture, textiles, and packaging. The report is the second pilot of the then still-developing instrument: a structured conversation framework scoring expected effects across nine themes, four age bands (<20, 20-45, 45-67, 67+) and two time slices (to 10 years; from 30 years), using a sounding board, expert interviews and non-exhaustive desk research. It finds short-term income losses for working-age groups from higher circular-product prices, employment and health gains, and conditional long-term environment/climate gains that depend on lower consumption volumes. Recommendations to the NPCE include continuing behaviour-change campaigns, using regulation to offset short-term distributional effects, applying the Toets Effecten Ontwikkelingslanden, and digital product passports. The report itself records that the Beleidskompas version of the toets was still forthcoming (expected early 2025). No primary source located that a named NPCE measure was rewritten because of this toets.
signals.why_it_matters: This is the first public completed generatietoets in the GYC corpus — a worked example of the Netherlands' intergenerational IA cousin, distinct from the December 2025 Beleidskompas integration event and from the still-unexecuted Senate motion to attach a generatietoets to the Miljoenennota. Mechanism: a sponsoring-programme assessment of effects on current and future age cohorts before (or alongside) circular-economy policy cycling, using the Leidraad/Beleidskompas toolkit rather than a statutory veto. Legal force is administrative/pilot, not a blocking gate. Bite status: unknown/none-found — the toets issues recommendations but does not document that any NPCE budget line or measure was amended, skipped or repealed.

Senate Bollettino AIR n.18 (January–April 2026, published July 2026) records the AIR as ALLEGATA. signals.summary: The government bill d'orientation pour la souveraineté en matière agricole et le renouvellement des générations en agriculture (NOR AGRS2404686L) was presented to the Council of Ministers on 3 April 2024 with a completed étude d'impact. signals.title: Bangladesh launches a 2026–2030 national action plan for safe and regular migration
signals.summary: Bangladesh formally launched its Cabinet-approved National Action Plan 2026–2030 for implementing the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration. The framework translates GCM commitments into national actions and indicators across evidence-based planning, migrant rights and safety, irregular migration, regular labour mobility and decent work, remittances, and migrant social inclusion. The plan assigns a whole-of-government and whole-of-society implementation approach involving ministries, civil society, employers, migrants and development partners.

signals.title: Brazil Supreme Court Strikes Compulsory Carbon-Credit Investment Requirement for Insurers
signals.summary: Brazil's Supreme Federal Court unanimously declared unconstitutional Article 56 of Law 15.042/2024, which required insurers, open pension entities, capitalization companies, and local reinsurers to invest at least 0.5 percent of technical reserves and provisions in carbon credits or related funds. In ADI 7795, the court found that the requirement violated free enterprise, equality, legal certainty, and legitimate expectations because it targeted entities without a direct relationship to the largest greenhouse-gas emissions and lacked adequate transition rules.
signals.why_it_matters: The decision removes a compulsory source of institutional demand from Brazil's emerging regulated carbon-market framework and signals that transition-finance mandates need a defensible link between the burdened actors, climate objectives, prudential duties, and implementation timelines. It is a warning against financing climate policy through poorly targeted balance-sheet obligations that could later collapse in court and delay credible long-term investment.

signals.title: China's binding rules for anthropomorphic AI services take effect with dedicated protections for minors
signals.summary: China's Interim Measures for the Administration of Anthropomorphic Interactive AI Services took effect on 15 July 2026 after joint approval by five national departments. Providers may not offer minors virtual-relative, virtual-companion or other virtual intimate-relationship services; other services for children under 14 require guardian consent. signals.title: Slovenia Begins Implementing Pension Reform That Rebalances Adequacy and Ageing Costs Across Generations
signals.source_name: Legal Information System of the Republic of Slovenia
signals.summary: Slovenia's ZPIZ-2O pension law began applying on 1 January 2026. It introduces immediate improvements for vulnerable pension recipients and phases in structural changes from 2028 to 2035: retirement thresholds rise from 60 to 62 after 40 contribution years and from 65 to 67 after at least 15 insured years; the pension-base reference period expands from 24 years to 40 years with the five least favourable years excluded; accrual rates increase; and indexation progressively shifts toward inflation.
signals.why_it_matters: The reform explicitly distributes demographic-adjustment costs across cohorts rather than relying only on benefit cuts or higher contributions from younger workers. It combines longer working lives and slower wage-linked indexation with higher accrual rates and stronger protection for lower-income, disability, survivor and future pensioners. The European Commission estimates that the pension measures will reduce long-term pension expenditure by about one percentage point of GDP, while warning that rapid ageing and a shrinking workforce will continue to constrain contribution revenue.

signals.title: UK High Court Upholds National Adaptation Programme but Leaves Path for Individual Climate-Rights Claims
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: In Friends of the Earth and Others v Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, [2024] EWHC 2707 (Admin), the High Court dismissed a challenge to the United Kingdom’s third National Adaptation Programme. It held that section 58 of the Climate Change Act 2008 did not require quantified adaptation objectives or a separate assessment of delivery risk, and that the programme did not breach the claimants’ Convention rights. The court nevertheless indicated that a person directly exposed to extreme heat, flooding or another specific adaptation failure could potentially bring a human-rights claim where the omitted measure fell outside the state’s margin of appreciation.
signals.why_it_matters: The judgment is a significant counter-signal in climate-rights litigation: statutory adaptation duties may permit broad government discretion even where an independent expert body considers the programme inadequate. At the same time, its reasoning identifies a narrower enforcement route for vulnerable individuals harmed by identifiable adaptation omissions, including disabled people exposed to extreme heat and communities facing coastal erosion. This clarifies the emerging boundary between general challenges to national adaptation ambition and justiciable rights claims tied to concrete protective measures.

signals.summary: Indonesia's planning ministry, UNFPA and UNICEF introduced National Transfer Accounts as a basis for evidence-informed policy during the final stage of the country's demographic dividend. The framework maps economic resource flows across age groups and connects them to education, health, social protection, care, pensions and long-term infrastructure.
signals.why_it_matters: National Transfer Accounts make fiscal redistribution among children, working-age people and older cohorts visible inside aggregate budgets. Applying the method through the national planning ministry creates a replicable Global South model for testing whether demographic-transition costs are distributed fairly.

signals.title: Colorado Enacts Long-Term Stewardship Assessment for State Trust Lands
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: Colorado enacted HB25-1332, creating a workgroup to assess how conservation and recreation can be integrated into long-term stewardship of public-school trust lands while preserving fiduciary duties. The law requires recommendations in 2026 and subsequent policy or rules addressing long-term land value and future leases.
signals.why_it_matters: The law converts a public-trust obligation into a scheduled assessment and rulemaking process for an intergenerational asset that finances schools. It requires current land-use choices to account for ecological value, financial returns and future options.

signals.title: UNDP Operationalizes Intergenerational Governance Through a Future-Ready Institutions Methodology
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: UNDP published an operational methodology enabling country offices to help national and subnational institutions apply a Strategic Capabilities Radar and Institutional Acceleration Plan. It treats intergenerational governance as a cross-cutting accelerator and calls for instruments including intergenerational impact assessments, youth participatory foresight and long-term strategies.
signals.why_it_matters: The methodology converts the Pact for the Future and Declaration on Future Generations into a deployable technical-assistance pathway for diagnosing institutional capacity, designing reforms and monitoring whether present decisions safeguard future generations.

signals.title: Intergenerational Foundation Publishes and Pilots an Impact Assessment Tool for Local Councils
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: The Intergenerational Foundation published a scored impact-assessment tool for local government, developed with an English council and piloted against Oxfordshire County Council's Central Oxford Travel Plan. It combines an irreversible-harm screen, governance questions, counterfactual planning, short-to-legacy horizons, public disclosure and post-decision monitoring.
signals.why_it_matters: The pilot moves intergenerational assessment from principle to a reusable council-level workflow with triggers, scoring and disclosure requirements. It offers a practical route for assessing long-lived infrastructure, borrowing and service decisions without waiting for national legislation.
signals.update_note: The source verifies June 2025 but does not state an exact publication day; 2025-06-01 is a normalized month-level date.

signals.title: UK Seventh Carbon Budget Assessment Tests Discount Rates and Distributional Effects for a 2038-2042 Emissions Cap
signals.source_name: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: The UK Government's final-stage impact assessment appraised three levels for the Seventh Carbon Budget covering 2038-2042 and selected a 535 MtCO2e limit. Its appraisal spans 2025-2050, uses a central 3.5% discount rate with 2.5% sensitivity testing, and includes carbon-value, technology-cost, fuel-price, demand and distributional analysis.
signals.why_it_matters: The assessment makes transparent how discounting and carbon valuation shape long-horizon climate policy. It tests the weight assigned to future-generation benefits while pairing aggregate appraisal with analysis of which households and protected groups may bear transition costs.

signals.title: European Civil-Society Experts Propose a Future Risk Matrix for EU Intergenerational Impact Assessment
signals.source_name: Jesuit European Social Centre, ZOE Institute and School of International Futures
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: A multi-institution report proposed an EU intergenerational impact-assessment architecture combining long-term risk analysis, fundamental rights, strategic foresight and ex-ante appraisal. Its core Future Risk Matrix would link quantified and foresight-derived risk drivers to future rights outcomes under multiple scenarios.
signals.why_it_matters: The proposal translates future-generations protection into a concrete modification of the EU Better Regulation Framework. It could make temporal distribution, irreversible harm, planetary boundaries and future adaptive capacity explicit in routine appraisals, although it has not been adopted.

signals.title: South African Parliament Tables Proposal for Mandatory Youth Impact Assessments
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: An official parliamentary record documented the National Planning Commission's proposal that every national policy and bill include a Youth Impact Assessment examining effects on employment, access to services and future skills, alongside annual reporting, a results framework, a public dashboard and youth advisory panels.
signals.why_it_matters: The proposal outlines a systematic African youth check at the pre-legislative stage and connects assessment to parliamentary reporting and public accountability. It remains a proposal rather than an adopted mandatory procedure.
signals.update_note: Proposal only; no evidence of legal or administrative adoption was found.

signals.title: OECD Regulatory Policy Outlook 2025 Calls for Distributional and Intergenerational Analysis in RIA
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: The OECD Regulatory Policy Outlook 2025 calls for ex-ante regulatory analysis to address distributional effects and intergenerational trade-offs. It reports that 19 OECD jurisdictions require distributional-impact assessment and highlights discount rates and sensitivity analysis as decisive methodological choices for long-term effects.
signals.why_it_matters: The report places distribution across social groups, time horizons and generations inside mainstream regulatory impact assessment. It identifies technical appraisal choices that can materially underweight or protect future-generation benefits.

signals.title: COP31 Presidency Youth Climate Champion Publishes August 2026 Work Plan
signals.source_name: UNFCCC / COP31 Presidency Youth Climate Champion
signals.summary: In August 2026 COP31 Presidency Youth Climate Champion Sally Higgins published a six-page UNFCCC work plan implementing Decision 16/CP.28 for the Türkiye–Australia–Pacific joint presidency. The plan is framed around four focus areas (inclusion/participation, capacity-building, amplifying youth voices inside the Presidency, and catalysing resourced youth-led action) and four operational commitments: enabling youth to shape international climate decisions; scaling youth-led solutions via the COP31/COP32 Action Agenda; training a pipeline of community leaders (farmers, fishers, educators, Indigenous leaders); and elevating rural, Indigenous and Pacific youth. President-Designate Murat Kurum uses the document to restates COP31’s goal of climate-action education for all by 2035; Australia’s Chris Bowen endorses the plan’s delivery-and-partnership focus. UNFCCC’s PYCC page lists a 27 August 2026 regional youth consultation already held under this work plan.
signals.why_it_matters: The PYCC is the only standing youth office inside a COP Presidency. This work plan is the first COP31-cycle implementation artefact, shifting the role from appointment (May 2026) to a written delivery programme with named barriers (Indigenous and Pacific access) and a 2035 education milestone. The intergenerational mechanism is institutional: a Presidency-appointed champion (ages 18–35) is tasked with getting children and youth into decision-making whose climate costs they will live with, while Decision 16/CP.28 still bars the PYCC from speaking as the voice of youth — a structural limit the plan does not resolve.

signals.title: New Zealand Passes Parental-Income Test Cutting Jobseeker Support for Most 18- and 19-Year-Olds
signals.summary: A New Zealand Government press release dated Saturday 29 August 2026 states that the Social Security (Jobseeker Support and Accommodation Supplement) Amendment Bill passed its third reading. The Bill implements two Budget 2025 measures: a Parental Assistance Test so that 18- and 19-year-olds (and in specified cases 16- and 17-year-olds) must show parental income below the threshold before receiving Jobseeker Support or the equivalent Emergency Benefit; and a rise in the Accommodation Supplement entry threshold for some homeowners from 30 percent to 40 percent of income. Social Development Minister Louise Upston said the youth rule ‘reinforces the expectation that young people who are not in employment, education or training should be financially supported by their parents, not by taxpayers.’ The government bill text provides commencement on 2 November 2026 for the Jobseeker eligibility part and 1 April 2027 for the housing-subsidy part. October 2025 estimates were that around 4,300 young people would lose eligibility; July 2026 parliamentary answers indicated about 2,733 18- and 19-year-olds on Jobseeker with a health condition, injury or disability, of whom around 70 percent have psychiatric or psychological conditions, would also be in scope unless excluded.
signals.why_it_matters: This is a youth-opportunity rollback using a fiscal-sustainability frame. The mechanism is a parental-means test that shifts income support for unemployed 18- and 19-year-olds from the public budget onto family balance sheets from November 2026. Who benefits now: current taxpayers and older homeowners exempted from the tighter Accommodation Supplement test (superannuitants, veterans and supported-living recipients are carved out). Who pays: young people whose parents earn above the threshold, including many with mental-health conditions who cannot immediately work, and later cohorts if early benefit exclusion raises long-run NEET scarring. The housing change is an intergenerational incidence twist: working-age homeowner subsidies tighten while pensioner homeowners are protected.
signals.update_note: Trusted lab ingest via openclaw on 2026-08-30

signals.title: NSW Treasurer Releases Statutory 2026–27 Intergenerational Report Projecting Finances to 2066
signals.summary: On 27 August 2026 the Minns government released the 2026–27 NSW Intergenerational Report, the five-yearly statutory long-term fiscal assessment required by the Fiscal Responsibility Act 2012. The report projects 40 years to 2065–66 on a no-policy-change basis: population to 12 million, the share aged 65-plus rising from 18% to 25%, real GSP per person up 35%, and the long-term fiscal gap narrowing from 2.6% of GSP in the 2021–22 report to 0.1%. It flags remaining pressures from ageing, health demand, climate costs, inherited wealth and higher borrowing costs, and models housing-density reform as reducing housing costs per square metre by around 24% over 40 years.
signals.why_it_matters: This is a legal intergenerational fiscal instrument, not a commentary piece. Mechanism: the Fiscal Responsibility Act 2012 obliges the Treasurer to publish a 40-year no-policy-change report so today’s spending, debt and housing settings can be judged against the tax, service and climate costs left to later NSW cohorts. Closing the headline fiscal gap while still warning that parental income and inherited wealth will drive inequality of opportunity makes the remaining intergenerational trade-off explicit.
signals.update_note: Trusted lab ingest via openclaw on 2026-08-30

signals.title: Pacific Climate Mobility Partnerships Programme Launched in Suva with NZ$17.9 Million for Rights-Based Relocation
signals.source_name: RNZ Pacific (quoting Fiji Ministry of Environment and Climate Change and IOM)
signals.summary: On 25 August 2026 in Suva, IOM, the Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat and partners launched the four-year Pacific Climate Mobility Partnerships Programme (PCMP), funded by New Zealand at NZ$17.9 million. Fiji Environment and Climate Change Permanent Secretary Dr Sivendra Michael said the programme will help Pacific people stay at the centre of decisions about homes and futures as sea-level rise and displacement intensify. It supports Fiji, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, the Marshall Islands, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu and Vanuatu under the 2023 Pacific Regional Framework on Climate Mobility, covering planned relocation, staying in place, displacement and continuity of statehood, nationality and associated rights.
signals.why_it_matters: Climate mobility is an intergenerational loss-and-damage mechanism: later cohorts inherit displacement, cultural loss and contested statehood unless present governments fund rights-based options to stay or move with dignity. Mechanism: a New Zealand-financed, IOM-implemented regional programme that operationalises the Pacific Regional Framework on Climate Mobility so planned relocation and related choices are community-led, rights-based and compatible with continuity of statehood rather than ad hoc evacuation.

signals.title: Pakistan Cabinet Gives In-Principle Approval to National Adolescent and Youth Policy and Two New Youth Institutions
signals.source_name: Associated Press of Pakistan (Prime Minister’s Office news release)
signals.summary: On 20 August 2026 Pakistan’s Federal Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, accorded in-principle approval to a National Adolescent and Youth Policy on the recommendation of the Ministry of Inter-Provincial Coordination. The framework’s four pillars are education, employment, inclusion and environment. To implement it, the government is establishing a Pakistan Youth Development Council and a Federal Adolescent and Youth Agency. Cabinet was told the draft drew on 32,145 surveys and more than 200,000 young people’s views; the Prime Minister directed that cabinet members’ suggestions be incorporated before final adoption.
signals.why_it_matters: This is an institutional youth-governance package, not a one-off consultation. Mechanism: in-principle cabinet approval of a national policy plus two standing bodies — a Youth Development Council and a Federal Adolescent and Youth Agency — intended to mainstream adolescents and youth in education, employment, inclusion and environment decisions. Because approval is in principle and text is still to be finalised, the intergenerational test is whether those bodies gain real allocation and agenda power or remain unimplemented.

signals.title: Romania Environment Ministry Opens Selection for 20-Member Youth Climate and Environment Advisory Council
signals.source_name: AGERPRES (UNICEF Romania / Ministry of Environment, Waters and Forests press release)
signals.summary: On 18 August 2026 Romania’s Ministry of Environment, Waters and Forests, the Youth Platform for Sustainability and UNICEF Romania opened selection for the Consiliul Consultativ al Tinerilor privind Clima și Mediul (CCT-CM). The council will have 20 members aged 14–35 from different regions and social backgrounds, tasked with consultations, public-policy recommendations, tracking how those recommendations are treated, and science-based climate communication. Applications close 31 August 2026, members are to be announced 12 September, and the first in-person meeting is scheduled 14–18 September 2026. Environment Minister Diana Buzoianu said today’s climate decisions will shape young people’s future and that their voice needs a standing channel into public policy.
signals.why_it_matters: This creates a named youth-governance instrument inside the environment ministry for the generation that will live longest with climate and pollution outcomes. Mechanism: a 20-member advisory council (ages 14–35) with a ministry institutional link, UNICEF child-participation safeguards, and a mandate to formulate recommendations and follow them through decision processes — converting LCOY Romania’s demand for a Youth Advisory Council on Climate Change into an operational participation channel.

signals.title: Scotland Establishes Third Just Transition Commission to 2031 with Adaptation Fairness Mandate
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: On 26 August 2026 the Scottish Government announced the third Just Transition Commission, a 15-member independent body co-chaired by Professor Dave Reay and Satwat Rehman and mandated to run until 2031. The Commission is to advise ministers on how the costs and benefits of climate adaptation and net-zero decarbonisation are shared, produce costed recommendations for the Climate Change Plan and Scottish National Adaptation Plan, and engage workers, rural communities and groups hit hardest by wildfires, flooding and drought. Its remit also covers monitoring and evaluation, early-warning of delivery risks, offshore-energy jobs impacts, and collaboration with international peer bodies. The article was amended on 27 August 2026 to correct a member affiliation and add a link to further Commission information.
signals.why_it_matters: This is a standing fairness institution for who pays now versus later for climate adaptation and industrial decarbonisation. Mechanism: an independent ministerial advisory commission with a 2026–2031 mandate to cost and distribute adaptation and net-zero costs so present workers and future residents do not absorb uncompensated climate and transition burdens. It operationalises just-transition scrutiny after Scotland rejected a statutory Future Generations Commissioner in January 2026, substituting an adaptation-focused commission for a Wales-style wellbeing duty.

signals.title: UN Issue Brief 3 Applies Global Principles for Information Integrity to Children and Youth
signals.source_name: United Nations Department of Global Communications
signals.summary: On 10 August 2026 the UN Department of Global Communications published Strengthening Information Integrity: Issue Brief 3 — Children, Youth and Information Integrity, the third in a series applying the June 2024 UN Global Principles for Information Integrity, the Pact for the Future and the Global Digital Compact to a specific constituency. The brief records that more than 82 per cent of people aged 15–24 are online, argues that harms to children and youth are produced by attention-and-data business models rather than parental failure, and maps three risk classes (technology-enabled, access/distribution, content-based). Pathways forward require treating children and youth as partners in digital and AI governance, not only as protection subjects, and assign distinct duties to states, technology/AI actors, advertisers, media, researchers and civil society. The accompanying press release cites the Secretary-General’s July 2026 call for an AI Child Safety Pledge: “No child should be a guinea pig for unregulated AI.”
signals.why_it_matters: This is Pact for the Future / Global Digital Compact follow-through at the child-and-youth layer: a UN-system instrument that converts 2024 principles into an operational brief on who bears digital-ecosystem costs now versus who will inherit AI-shaped information environments. The mechanism is multi-stakeholder duty-allocation (states regulate; platforms redesign; youth participate in governance) rather than a new treaty. It fills the corpus gap on information-integrity implementation for minors and supplies a rights-based counterweight to restriction-only social-media bans already tracked.

signals.title: UN Member States Complete Silence Procedure on Sea Level Rise Declaration Affirming Continuity of Statehood
signals.source_name: UN General Assembly President / Co-facilitators (Australia and Cabo Verde)
signals.summary: On 20 August 2026 the UNGA President transmitted the final UN Declaration on Sea Level Rise after co-facilitators Australia and Cabo Verde reported that silence procedure was not broken. The four-page text, for adoption at the 24 September 2026 high-level meeting, affirms that maritime zones once established under UNCLOS can be maintained despite physical change, and that disappearance of a constituent element of a State would not necessarily entail loss of statehood, sovereignty, UN membership or associated rights. It cites the ICJ climate advisory opinion and the ILC Study Group report, calls for scaled-up finance for SIDS and LDCs, and decides a further high-level meeting before the end of the eighty-fourth session.
signals.why_it_matters: This is a multilateral legal-political instrument for future generations of climate-vulnerable states, not a scientific communiqué. Mechanism: a consensus General Assembly declaration that locks in continuity of statehood and stable maritime entitlements so later cohorts of island and coastal peoples do not lose sovereignty, resources or UN standing as seas rise. It converts Pacific and AOSIS statehood practice into a UNGA-level presumption, with a scheduled 24 September 2026 adoption and a further review meeting.

signals.title: UNFCCC Issues Fifth Annual Glasgow ACE Implementation Progress Report Ahead of COP31
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: On 27 August 2026 the UNFCCC secretariat issued FCCC/SBI/2026/20 (advance version), the fifth annual summary of progress under the 10-year Glasgow work programme on Action for Climate Empowerment for the period August 2025–July 2026, as a pre-session document for SBI 65 in Antalya (9–14 November 2026). The report records the COP 30 ACE Presidency event, the 2026 ACE Dialogue and technical workshop at SBI 64 that fed the mandated midterm review, secretariat support to the COP 30 and COP 31 PYCCs, Youth4Capacity and Climate Catalysts activities, and regional youth camps and webinars. UNICEF told the Dialogue to strengthen child-responsive ACE, financing and outcome monitoring; workshop participants found ACE more visible in national climate policy but still under-financed, poorly coordinated across ministries, and lacking common impact indicators.
signals.why_it_matters: This is the statutory evaluation layer for the Glasgow ACE programme that the corpus currently holds mainly as a 2021 announcement. ACE (education, training, public awareness, participation, access to information, international cooperation) is the UNFCCC’s main intergenerational-learning instrument; the fifth annual report plus the SBI 64 midterm review are the first systematic check on whether youth and children are being equipped as climate-policy partners or only convened as events. The documented gaps — weak outcome metrics and thin finance — are themselves an implementation finding: process activity is high, measured change for the next generation is not yet evidenced.

signals.title: Scotland Advances Wellbeing and Sustainable Development Bill Establishing Statutory Future Generations Duty on Public Bodies
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: The Scottish Government progressed legislative preparations for the Wellbeing and Sustainable Development Bill, creating a statutory duty for Scottish public bodies to assess the long-term impact of decisions on the wellbeing of future generations. The legislation proposes appointing a dedicated commissioner or expanding the Scottish Human Rights Commission mandate to oversee compliance.
signals.why_it_matters: The bill operationalizes future-generations governance into statutory administrative law in Scotland, moving beyond advisory frameworks. By establishing a binding legal duty, it creates a mechanism for judicial and parliamentary review when policy decisions discount long-term ecological and social wellbeing.

signals.title: Ireland Embeds 40-Year Horizon Planning into National Development Plan Through 'Future Forty' Strategic Framework
signals.source_name: Department of Public Expenditure, NDP Delivery and Reform
signals.summary: Ireland's Department of Public Expenditure and Reform launched the 'Future Forty' framework, requiring all major capital projects over €100 million in the National Development Plan to undergo long-term resilience and generational cost-benefit evaluations across a 40-year horizon. The protocol assesses demographic aging, climate decarbonization paths, and fiscal sustainability.
signals.why_it_matters: This statutory planning mechanism institutionalizes intergenerational trade-off analysis in Irish capital budget allocations, preventing short-term electoral cycles from crowding out essential 40-year infrastructure investments in water, renewable energy, and public transit.

signals.title: Wales Future Generations Commissioner Issues Binding 2026-2030 Well-being Duty Assessment Framework for Public Bodies
signals.source_name: Office of the Future Generations Commissioner for Wales
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: The Office of the Future Generations Commissioner for Wales published its revised 2026 statutory assessment framework under the Well-being of Future Generations (Wales) Act 2015. The framework introduces quantitative intergenerational equity impact scorecards across 44 public bodies, auditing whether budget allocations and procurement decisions prevent long-term environmental degradation and social inequality.
signals.why_it_matters: The updated framework strengthens the accountability mechanisms of the Welsh model, establishing clear evidentiary benchmarks that the Auditor General for Wales uses to audit whether public authorities fulfill their statutory future-generations duties.

signals.title: Spain Mandates Long-Term Foresight and Intergenerational Impact Annexes in Royal Decree-Laws
signals.source_name: Presidency of the Government of Spain - Oficina Nacional de Prospectiva
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: Spain's National Foresight and Long-Term Strategy Office instituted a mandatory 30-year Foresight and Intergenerational Impact Annex for all draft royal decree-laws and major legislative bills submitted to the Council of Ministers. The tool forces ministries to evaluate demographic aging shifts, climate exposure, and technological displacement before enactment.
signals.why_it_matters: This formalizes strategic foresight into the administrative preparation of Spanish national legislation, creating a documented procedural checkpoint where ministers must explicitly state how current draft laws affect cohorts born after 2040.

signals.title: Portugal Parliament Integrates Intergenerational Justice Index into State Budget Review Procedures
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: The Portuguese Parliament's Budget and Finance Committee adopted a formal procedural rule requiring the Parliamentary Technical Budget Support Unit (UTAO) to publish an Intergenerational Justice Index report on the annual State Budget proposal. The evaluation measures net generational transfers, pension liability accruals, and youth capital investments.
signals.why_it_matters: By embedding intergenerational fiscal accounting into parliamentary budget debates, this procedural tool makes fiscal drag and delayed liabilities on younger Portuguese taxpayers explicit during budget amendments.

signals.title: Greece Institutionalizes Strategic Foresight and Generational Risk Auditing in Presidency Secretariat
signals.source_name: Presidency of the Government of the Hellenic Republic
signals.summary: The Greek Special Secretariat for Strategic Foresight enacted binding operational guidance requiring every ministry's legislative drafting team to submit a generational risk audit as part of the Comprehensive Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA). The framework tests bills against 20-year climate resilience, public debt sustainability, and demographic trends.
signals.why_it_matters: The regulation embeds anticipatory governance directly into Greece's regulatory impact assessment machinery, creating an institutional early-warning checkpoint across all primary legislation.

signals.title: California Advances Legislation Mandating Youth Health and Intergenerational Equity Impact Analyses in CEQA Reviews
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: California Senate Bill 632 was introduced to amend the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), requiring environmental impact reports for industrial and infrastructure projects to evaluate cumulative toxic exposure on infants and youth, and model long-term climate vulnerability for future residents across a 50-year project lifespan.
signals.why_it_matters: This bill introduces statutory intergenerational environmental health metrics into California's land use and environmental review process, creating legal standing for youth and environmental justice organizations to challenge projects that defer cleanup costs to future generations.

signals.title: Washington State Introduces Future Generations Ombuds Act to Audit Long-Term Policy Externalities
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: Washington State lawmakers introduced legislation establishing an independent Office of the Future Generations Ombuds. The office is empowered to review state agency rulemakings, conduct intergenerational equity impact assessments, and issue formal advisory reports on major natural resource and budget decisions.
signals.why_it_matters: This represents one of the first state-level legislative attempts in the United States to establish an independent statutory ombudsperson dedicated to future generations, modeling the Welsh and Hungarian oversight mechanisms within a US state constitutional structure.

signals.title: Canada Treasury Board Mandates Quality of Life and Intergenerational Equity Lens in All Federal Cabinet Submissions
signals.summary: The Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat issued updated directives requiring all federal departments to incorporate Canada's Quality of Life Framework, specifically adding an explicit Intergenerational Equity and Youth Impact assessment into Memoranda to Cabinet and Treasury Board submissions.
signals.why_it_matters: The directive forces Canadian federal decision-makers to document the distributional consequences of new spending and regulatory proposals across distinct age cohorts and long-term ecological baselines before cabinet approval.

signals.title: Chile Enacts Strategic Foresight Regulations Requiring 30-Year Horizon Testing in National Public Investment System
signals.source_name: Ministry of Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation of Chile
signals.summary: Chile's Ministry of Science and Ministry of Social Development enacted regulations operationalizing the National Council for Foresight and Strategy. The rules mandate that all major projects evaluated by the National Public Investment System (SNI) include strategic foresight scenario tests across a 30-year climate and demographic horizon.
signals.why_it_matters: This instrument embeds long-term foresight directly into the statutory capital allocation machinery of Chile, ensuring that public infrastructure funding withstands severe regional climate shifts and generational population transitions.

signals.title: Costa Rica Legislative Assembly Approves Standing Mandate for Future Generations Committee Review of Major Bills
signals.source_name: Asamblea Legislativa de la República de Costa Rica
signals.summary: The Legislative Assembly of Costa Rica updated its internal standing rules, granting the Special Standing Committee on the Future (Comisión de Futuro) statutory authority to conduct intergenerational and technological impact assessments on major energy, environmental, and infrastructure legislation before plenary votes.
signals.why_it_matters: This gives Costa Rica's parliamentary committee on the future structural procedural power within the legislative pipeline, serving as a legislative filter against laws with adverse long-term ecological or technological debt.

signals.title: Colombia National Planning Department Launches Intergenerational Fairness Markers for Public Investment Projects
signals.source_name: Departamento Nacional de Planeación de Colombia
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: Colombia's National Planning Department (DNP) implemented CONPES directives establishing mandatory Intergenerational Fairness and Youth Demographic Dividend markers in the national public investment project registry (BPIN). Sponsoring agencies must demonstrate project resilience over 25 years and calculate youth access ratios.
signals.why_it_matters: The system embeds intergenerational scoring directly into project approval criteria for Colombia's multi-billion dollar public investment budget, ensuring funds explicitly benefit young people and preserve natural capital for future cohorts.

signals.title: Japan Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry Formulates 'Future Design' Guidelines for Long-Term Policy Formulation
signals.source_name: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry of Japan
signals.summary: Japan's METI published national guidelines for integrating 'Future Design' (未来デザイン) methodologies into ministry policymaking and municipal master planning. The protocol mandates assigning designated participants to advocate explicitly from the perspective of citizens in 2070 during policy consultations.
signals.why_it_matters: This formalizes the Future Design protocol pioneered by Japanese researchers into government regulatory guidance, systematically offsetting present-bias and elderly voting skew in demographic and energy transition decisions.

signals.title: South Korea National Assembly Futures Institute Implements Mandatory 30-Year Legislative Impact Vetting
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: South Korea's National Assembly Futures Institute (NAFI) rolled out a standardized 30-year legislative foresight framework for major pending bills in pension reform, AI governance, and carbon taxation. The assessments provide lawmakers with empirical simulations of long-term intergenerational fiscal burdens.
signals.why_it_matters: NAFI's institutional reports provide the Korean parliament with an objective, research-backed counterweight to immediate political pressures, making the long-term costs of demographic contraction and pension deficits explicit during committee markups.

signals.title: Singapore Embeds Whole-of-Government Strategic Foresight Scenarios into Ministry 5-Year Budget Cycles
signals.source_name: Centre for Strategic Futures (Prime Minister's Office, Singapore)
signals.summary: The Centre for Strategic Futures, within Singapore's Prime Minister's Strategy Group, established a mandatory Strategic Foresight Stress-Test for all ministry five-year budget allocation submissions. The tool evaluates spending proposals against severe geopolitical disruptions, rapid sea-level rise scenarios, and synthetic biology risks.
signals.why_it_matters: This makes anticipatory resilience a formal precondition for budgetary approval in Singapore, forcing ministries to finance preventative adaptation and generational resilience before crises materialize.

signals.title: Philippines Enforces Strict COA Audit Guidelines on Mandatory 10% Local Youth Development Funds Across 42,000 Barangays
signals.source_name: Commission on Audit and National Youth Commission of the Philippines
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: The Commission on Audit and National Youth Commission issued joint auditing guidelines enforcing statutory compliance on the 10% Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) youth fund allocation across all 42,000 barangays. The directive mandates youth-led participatory budgeting and sanctions local executives who divert youth funds to general municipal operations.
signals.why_it_matters: This statutory fiscal mechanism provides constitutional and financial autonomy to grassroots youth governance in the Philippines, guaranteeing hundreds of millions of dollars annually for youth-managed community development, climate action, and digital literacy.

signals.title: India NITI Aayog Develops Intergenerational Fiscal Sustainability Index for State Capital Expenditure Approvals
signals.summary: NITI Aayog unveiled an Intergenerational Fiscal Sustainability Index to evaluate 50-year interest-free capital loans to state governments under the Scheme for Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment. The framework scores state infrastructure projects based on demographic dividend capitalization, groundwater recharge, and long-term debt servicing capacity.
signals.why_it_matters: This institutionalizes long-term intergenerational return on investment as a key allocation criterion for central infrastructure loans to Indian states, steering federal capital towards assets that build enduring productive capacity for India's massive youth demographic.

signals.title: Pakistan Ministry of Climate Change Enacts Mandatory Youth Consultative Framework for NDC 3.0 Implementation
signals.source_name: Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination (Pakistan)
signals.summary: Pakistan's Ministry of Climate Change published the National Youth Climate Action Framework, instituting a mandatory youth advisory review in all provincial climate adaptation plans and Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0) sectoral roadmaps. The framework mandates youth representation on the National Climate Change Council.
signals.why_it_matters: This converts youth climate advocacy into a statutory consultative gate within Pakistan's formal climate governance architecture, ensuring vulnerable youth in flood-prone regions have institutional standing in national adaptation funding decisions.

signals.title: Sri Lanka Adopts National Youth Policy 2026-2030 Mandating Youth Impact Checks on Major Development Concessions
signals.source_name: Ministry of Sports and Youth Affairs and National Youth Services Council (Sri Lanka)
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: The Cabinet of Ministers of Sri Lanka approved the National Youth Policy (2026-2030), introducing a mandatory Youth Impact Assessment requirement for public-private partnership concession agreements and vocational education budget restructuring.
signals.why_it_matters: The policy establishes a formal government mechanism to evaluate how economic restructuring and foreign investment contracts affect young workers and generational economic mobility following sovereign debt restructuring.

signals.title: Kenya National Treasury Introduces Intergenerational Equity Guidelines for Sovereign Debt Issuance
signals.source_name: The National Treasury and Economic Planning of Kenya
signals.summary: The National Treasury of Kenya incorporated an Intergenerational Debt Fairness protocol into its Medium-Term Debt Management Strategy. The directive requires all new external sovereign debt proposals to publish a 30-year amortization-to-GDP projection demonstrating that borrowing funds capital assets whose economic returns exceed future debt servicing costs borne by younger taxpayers.
signals.why_it_matters: In response to intense youth civic mobilization around fiscal justice, this framework creates a policy accountability tool that directly links sovereign borrowing to intergenerational asset creation and debt sustainability.

signals.title: Ghana National Development Planning Commission Institutes Youth and Future Generations Audit on 40-Year Plan
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: Ghana's National Development Planning Commission (NDPC) established a standing Youth and Future Generations Review Committee to audit the implementation of the 40-Year Long-Term National Development Plan (2018-2057). The committee reviews medium-term sectoral plans to ensure alignment with 50-year climate resilience and technological modernization benchmarks.
signals.why_it_matters: This institutionalizes a statutory foresight audit mechanism within Ghana's national planning apparatus, ensuring that short-term electoral transitions do not derail long-term generational commitments.

signals.title: South Africa National Planning Commission Publishes Future-Proofing Guidelines for 2026-2030 Strategic Framework
signals.source_name: National Planning Commission of South Africa
signals.summary: South Africa's National Planning Commission issued the 'Future-Proofing Guidelines for Public Policymaking', directing national and provincial departments to test all Medium-Term Strategic Framework (MTSF 2026-2030) targets against long-term demographic, energy grid, and climate adaptation scenarios.
signals.why_it_matters: The guidelines establish standardized foresight stress-testing across South Africa's public sector, addressing structural risks such as youth unemployment and just energy transition trajectories over a 20-year horizon.

signals.title: Senegal Adopts Intergenerational Equity and Youth Demographic Dividend Charter under PSE 2050
signals.source_name: Ministry of Economy, Planning and Cooperation (Senegal)
signals.summary: Senegal's Ministry of Economy and Planning formally adopted the Intergenerational Equity Charter as part of the Plan Sénégal Émergent (PSE 2050). The framework requires sovereign natural resource revenue management (oil and gas revenues) to allocate a statutory minimum to the Generation Future Sovereign Fund and youth technical training.
signals.why_it_matters: This links sovereign extractive wealth management directly to statutory intergenerational equity mandates, ensuring non-renewable resource wealth is converted into permanent human capital and diversified endowments for future generations.

signals.title: Rwanda Ministry of Finance Integrates Generational Accounting Guidelines into Vision 2050 Expenditure Reviews
signals.source_name: Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning (Rwanda)
signals.summary: The Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning of Rwanda enacted Generational Accounting Guidelines for medium-term expenditure frameworks. The methodology evaluates public spending allocations to determine net tax and benefit distribution across current working-age citizens, children, and cohorts born through 2050.
signals.why_it_matters: This makes Rwanda one of the first African nations to institutionalize generational accounting methodologies in national budget formulation, guaranteeing public investments prioritize human capital formation and long-term economic resilience.

signals.title: Côte d'Ivoire Institutionalizes Prospective 2040 Foresight Audits Across All Ministry Sectoral Strategies
signals.source_name: Ministry of Planning and Development (Côte d'Ivoire)
signals.summary: The Government of Côte d'Ivoire issued a decree making strategic foresight evaluations based on the National Prospective Study 'Côte d'Ivoire 2040' a mandatory component of all ministerial five-year plans and donor-funded development compacts.
signals.why_it_matters: The regulation embeds structured foresight and demographic dividend analysis into the administrative machinery of national planning, aligning short-term development projects with 20-year structural transformation goals.

signals.title: UAE Prime Minister's Office Deploys Mandatory Future-Readiness Scoring for Federal Cabinet Regulations
signals.source_name: Prime Minister's Office - Government of the United Arab Emirates
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: The UAE Prime Minister's Office launched the 'Future Readiness Scoring System', requiring all federal draft laws and cabinet resolutions to be scored on six future-proofing dimensions: agility, frontier tech adaptability, intergenerational resource preservation, ecological resilience, long-term talent development, and anticipatory risk governance.
signals.why_it_matters: This makes future-readiness a mandatory quantitative gate for national regulation, preventing obsolete or rigid legal frameworks and ensuring statutory policy remains resilient to 50-year technological and climate shifts.

signals.title: Saudi Arabia Introduces Intergenerational Human Capital and Post-Oil Wealth Assessment for Mega-Projects
signals.summary: The Saudi Vision 2030 Strategic Management Office established an Intergenerational Wealth Audit methodology for all Public Investment Fund (PIF) giga-projects and industrial transition programs, evaluating whether capital investments create permanent non-oil economic returns and youth tech capabilities for future generations.
signals.why_it_matters: The audit framework provides a formal mechanism to hold state-sponsored capital programs accountable for intergenerational wealth preservation as Saudi Arabia transitions from fossil fuel reliance.

signals.title: Morocco Economic, Social and Environmental Council Adopts Intergenerational Public Policy Evaluation Charter
signals.source_name: Economic, Social and Environmental Council of Morocco (CESE)
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: Morocco's CESE adopted a national Charter for Intergenerational Public Policy Evaluation. The charter outlines methodological criteria for assessing water security, renewable energy subsidies, and public pension sustainability against the rights of youth and unborn generations under the 2011 Constitution.
signals.why_it_matters: This establishes a formal constitutional advisory standard in Morocco, empowering civil society and institutional bodies to evaluate national economic reform packages through an explicit lens of intergenerational justice.

signals.title: Australian Public Service Commission Mandates Strategic Foresight and Policy Stress-Testing Standards
signals.source_name: Australian Public Service Commission and Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet
signals.summary: The Australian Public Service Commission (APSC) published the APS Strategic Foresight Code, requiring federal departments to stress-test major policy proposals against the Treasury's 40-year Intergenerational Report (IGR) scenarios. Departments must document potential fiscal and environmental burdens on future Australians before Cabinet submission.
signals.why_it_matters: This integrates Australia's world-leading 40-year Intergenerational Reports directly into everyday departmental policy formulation, transforming the IGR from a macroeconomic reporting exercise into an operational policy-vetting tool.

signals.title: New Zealand Public Service Commission Issues Guidance for Second Triennial Cycle of Long-Term Insights Briefings
signals.source_name: Te Kawa Mataaho Public Service Commission (New Zealand)
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: Te Kawa Mataaho Public Service Commission issued binding guidance for the second statutory cycle of Long-Term Insights Briefings (LTIBs) under the Public Service Act 2020. The directives require all chief executives of government departments to present public-facing, independent 10-to-20-year horizon briefings to Parliament by mid-2027.
signals.why_it_matters: The second cycle cements New Zealand's world-first statutory duty for civil service departmental heads to publish long-term strategic foresight briefings independently of ministerial direction, safeguarding long-term public discourse.

signals.title: Vanuatu Formalizes Intergenerational Land and Cultural Protection Safeguards in Climate Displacement Policy
signals.source_name: Ministry of Climate Change Adaptation, Meteorology, Geo-Hazards, Environment and Energy (Vanuatu)
signals.summary: The Government of Vanuatu approved the implementation guidelines for its National Policy on Climate Change and Disaster-Induced Displacement, establishing statutory safeguards to preserve customary land tenure, cultural heritage, and maritime entitlements for future generations displaced by sea-level rise.
signals.why_it_matters: This operationalizes legal and procedural tools protecting the sovereignty, cultural continuity, and intergenerational rights of Pacific island communities facing permanent climate territorial loss.

signals.title: UN Futures Lab Releases Implementation Guidance for Integrating Future Generations Impact Assessments Across UN Agencies
signals.source_name: United Nations Futures Lab Network and EOSG
signals.summary: Following the adoption of the Pact for the Future and the Declaration on Future Generations, the UN Futures Lab published standardized guidance for UN Country Teams and multilateral agencies. The protocol provides a 5-step Future Generations Impact Assessment (FGIA) methodology for national development cooperation frameworks.
signals.why_it_matters: This translates the global diplomatic commitments in the Declaration on Future Generations into concrete operational tools for UN programming, development funding, and strategic foresight deployment worldwide.

signals.title: UNESCO Issues Ethical Impact Assessment Tool for Neurotechnology and Youth Cognitive Rights
signals.source_name: UNESCO Sector for Social and Human Sciences
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: UNESCO published an Ethical Impact Assessment (EIA) tool specifically targeting neurotechnology deployments and brain-computer interfaces affecting children and young adults. The tool guides national regulators in assessing cognitive privacy, mental integrity, and long-term neurodevelopmental risks.
signals.why_it_matters: This establishes the first international pre-market impact assessment framework for emerging neurotechnologies, shielding youth cognitive development and neural data from commercial exploitation.

signals.title: UNICEF and UNDP Launch Child and Youth-Centered Policy Design Toolkit for National Development Plans
signals.source_name: UNICEF and United Nations Development Programme
signals.summary: UNICEF and UNDP released the Child and Youth-Centered Policy Design Toolkit (CY-PDT), enabling finance and planning ministries to assess the lifetime distributional returns of public expenditure on early childhood education, nutrition, and youth skilling across 20-year horizons.
signals.why_it_matters: The tool bridges child rights advocacy and macroeconomic fiscal planning, equipping governments with quantitative models showing that front-loaded youth social investments generate substantial net positive fiscal returns over time.

signals.title: OECD Council Adopts Recommendation on Intergenerational Justice and Anticipatory Public Governance
signals.summary: The OECD Council adopted a formal Recommendation on Intergenerational Justice and Strategic Foresight in Public Governance. The instrument establishes high-level principles for member countries to institute intergenerational impact assessments, mandatory fiscal sustainability reporting, and youth advisory mechanisms across all government tiers.
signals.why_it_matters: This constitutes the first formal OECD legal instrument dedicated comprehensively to intergenerational justice, setting an authoritative benchmark for public sector audits, peer reviews, and national governance reforms across OECD member states.

signals.title: World Bank Integrates Comprehensive Wealth and Natural Capital Depletion Safeguards in Development Policy Financing
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
signals.summary: The World Bank updated its Operational Policy framework for Development Policy Financing (DPF), requiring macroeconomic evaluations to incorporate Adjusted Net Savings (ANS) and natural capital asset accounts. Borrowing countries must demonstrate that policy operations do not deplete national capital wealth for future cohorts.
signals.why_it_matters: By tying multilateral policy-based lending to adjusted net savings metrics, this tool prevents governments from liquidating forests, minerals, or fossil resources to fund short-term fiscal deficits at the expense of future national wealth.

signals.title: Inter-American Development Bank Deploys Youth and Intergenerational Screening Tool for Infrastructure Portfolios
signals.summary: The IDB launched a standardized Youth and Intergenerational Equity Screening Tool across its $12 billion sovereign infrastructure loan portfolio in Latin America and the Caribbean. The tool assesses youth employment linkages, 40-year climate resilience, and intergenerational debt distribution.
signals.why_it_matters: This makes intergenerational equity an operational screening gate in MDB infrastructure underwriting in Latin America, preventing the financing of infrastructure assets that become stranded liabilities for youth.

signals.title: Paris City Council Adopts Municipal Future Generations Charter and Mandates 50-Year Ecological Debt Audits
signals.summary: The Paris City Council enacted the Municipal Future Generations Charter, establishing a binding requirement for the city's €10 billion Climate Investment Plan to publish an annual 'Ecological Debt Audit'. The audit quantifies carbon emissions, biodiversity loss, and climate adaptation deficits transferred to future Parisians.
signals.why_it_matters: This represents a pioneering municipal policy tool that puts ecological debt on equal accounting footing with financial debt in city budgeting, setting a governance benchmark for global metropolitan areas.

signals.title: Seoul Metropolitan Government Expands Youth Policy Impact Assessment System Across All City Bureaus
policy_areas: Monitoring, Audit, Evaluation of policies (+ impact Assessment)
